32.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
nirguṇaḥ śāśvato devas tvayā prokto divākaraḥ
punar dvādaśadhā jātaḥ śruto 'smābhis tvayoditaḥ //
32.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
निर्गुणः शाश्वतो देवस् त्वया प्रोक्तो दिवाकरः
पुनर् द्वादशधा जातः श्रुतो ऽस्माभिस् त्वयोदितः ॥

32.s:
sa kathaṃ tejaso raśmiḥ striyā garbhe mahādyutiḥ
saṃbhūto bhāskaro jātas tatra naḥ saṃśayo mahān //
32.d:
स कथं तेजसो रश्मिः स्त्रिया गर्भे महाद्युतिः
संभूतो भास्करो जातस् तत्र नः संशयो महान् ॥
32.m: How did that mass of splendour, the sun of great radiance, come to be born in the womb of a woman? Concerning that, we have a great doubt.

32.s:
brahmovāca
dakṣasya hi sutāḥ śreṣṭhā babhūvuḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ śobhanāḥ
aditir ditir danuś caiva vinatādyās tathaiva ca //
32.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
दक्षस्य हि सुताः श्रेष्ठा बभूवुः षष्टिः शोभनाः
अदितिर् दितिर् दनुश् चैव विनताद्यास् तथैव च ॥
32.m:
Brahmā said:
Indeed, Dakṣa had sixty excellent, beautiful daughters:
Aditi, Diti, Danu, and also Vinatā and the others.

32.s:
dakṣas tāḥ pradadau kanyāḥ kaśyapāya trayodaśa
aditir janayām āsa devāṃs tribhuvaneśvarān //
32.d:
दक्षस् ताः प्रददौ कन्याः कश्यपाय त्रयोदश
अदितिर् जनयाम् आस देवांस् त्रिभुवनेश्वरान् ॥
32.m:
Dakṣa gave thirteen of those maidens to Kaśyapa.
Aditi gave birth to the gods, lords of the three worlds.

32.s:
daityān ditir danuś cogrān dānavān baladarpitān
vinatādyās tathā cānyāḥ suṣuvuḥ sthānujaṅgamān //
32.d:
दैत्यान् दितिर् दनुश् चोग्रान् दानवान् बलदर्पितान्
विनताद्यास् तथा चान्याः सुषुवुः स्थानुजङ्गमान् ॥
32.m:
Diti gave birth to the Daityas, and Danu to the fierce Dānavas arrogant in their strength;
and Vinatā and the others gave birth to stationary and moving creatures.

32.s:
tasyātha putradauhitraiḥ pautradauhitrakādibhiḥ
vyāptam etaj jagat sarvaṃ teṣāṃ tāsāṃ ca vai mune //
32.d:
तस्याथ पुत्रदौहित्रैः पौत्रदौहित्रकादिभिः
व्याप्तम् एतज् जगत् सर्वं तेषां तासां च वै मुने ॥
32.m:
Then, O sage, by their sons and daughters' sons, their grandsons, great-grandsons, and the rest,
all this universe was pervaded by those male and female beings.

32.s:
teṣāṃ kaśyapaputrāṇāṃ pradhānā devatāgaṇāḥ
sāttvikā rājasāś cānye tāmasāś ca gaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ //
32.d:
तेषां कश्यपपुत्राणां प्रधाना देवतागणाः
सात्त्विका राजसाश् चान्ये तामसाश् च गणाः स्मृताः ॥
32.m:
Among those sons of Kaśyapa, the hosts of deities are the foremost;
they are taught to be sāttvika hosts, while others are rājasika and tāmasika.

32.s:
devān yajñabhujaś cakre tathā tribhuvaneśvarān
sraṣṭā brahmavidāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ parameṣṭhī prajāpatiḥ //
32.d:
देवान् यज्ञभुजश् चक्रे तथा त्रिभुवनेश्वरान्
स्रष्टा ब्रह्मविदां श्रेष्ठः परमेष्ठी प्रजापतिः ॥
32.m:
The creator, the best of knowers of the Veda, the highest lord, the lord of creatures,
made the gods the eaters of sacrificial offerings and the lords of the three worlds.

32.s:
tān abādhanta sahitāḥ sāpatnyād daityadānavāḥ
tato nirākṛtān putrān daiteyair dānavais tathā //
32.d:
तान् अबाधन्त सहिताः सापत्न्याद् दैत्यदानवाः
ततो निराकृतान् पुत्रान् दैतेयैर् दानवैस् तथा ॥
32.m:
Because of rivalry among co-wives, the Daityas and Dānavas united to torment them.
Then seeing her sons expelled by the Daityas and Dānavas,

32.s:
hataṃ tribhuvanaṃ dṛṣṭvā aditir munisattamāḥ
ācchinad yajñabhāgāṃś ca kṣudhā saṃpīḍitān bhṛśam //
32.d:
हतं त्रिभुवनं दृष्ट्वा अदितिर् मुनिसत्तमाः
आच्छिनद् यज्ञभागांश् च क्षुधा संपीडितान् भृशम् ॥
32.m: and seeing the three worlds overcome, O best of sages, and their sacrificial shares snatched away, [and her sons] greatly afflicted with hunger,

32.s:
ārādhanāya savituḥ paraṃ yatnaṃ pracakrame
ekāgrā niyatāhārā paraṃ niyamam āsthitā
tuṣṭāva tejasāṃ rāśiṃ gaganasthaṃ divākaram //
32.d:
आराधनाय सवितुः परं यत्नं प्रचक्रमे
एकाग्रा नियताहारा परं नियमम् आस्थिता
तुष्टाव तेजसां राशिं गगनस्थं दिवाकरम् ॥
32.m:
Aditi undertook supreme effort to propitiate the sun.
Single-minded, restricting her diet, and established in the highest discipline,
she praised the sun standing in the sky, a mass of splendours.

32.s:
aditir uvāca
namas tubhyaṃ paraṃ sūkṣmaṃ supuṇyaṃ bibhrate 'tulam
dhāma dhāmavatām īśaṃ dhāmādhāraṃ ca śāśvatam //
32.d:
अदितिर् उवाच
नमस् तुभ्यं परं सूक्ष्मं सुपुण्यं बिभ्रते ऽतुलम्
धाम धामवताम् ईशं धामाधारं च शाश्वतम् ॥
32.m:
Aditi said:
Salutations to you, who bear the supreme, subtle, highly meritorious, incomparable
abode, lord of the luminous, eternal foundation of light!

32.s:
jagatām upakārāya tvām ahaṃ staumi gopate
ādadānasya yad rūpaṃ tīvraṃ tasmai namāmy aham //
32.d:
जगताम् उपकाराय त्वाम् अहं स्तौमि गोपते
आददानस्य यद् रूपं तीव्रं तस्मै नमाम्य् अहम् ॥
32.m:
For the welfare of the worlds I praise you, lord of rays!
To that intense form of yours which takes up [moisture], I bow.

32.s:
grahītum aṣṭamāsena kālenāmbumayaṃ rasam
bibhratas tava yad rūpam atitīvraṃ natāsmi tat //
32.d:
ग्रहीतुम् अष्टमासेन कालेनाम्बुमयं रसम्
बिभ्रतस् तव यद् रूपम् अतितीव्रं नतास्मि तत् ॥
32.m: To that excessively fiery form of yours which is assumed to seize watery essence over the course of eight months, I bow down.

32.s:
sametam agnisomābhyāṃ namas tasmai guṇātmane
yad rūpam ṛgyajuḥsāmnām aikyena tapate tava //
32.d:
समेतम् अग्निसोमाभ्यां नमस् तस्मै गुणात्मने
यद् रूपम् ऋग्यजुःसाम्नाम् ऐक्येन तपते तव ॥
32.m:
United with fire and Soma, salutations to that embodiment of qualities,
to that form of yours which burns through the unity of the Ṛc, Yajus, and Sāman!

32.s:
viśvam etat trayīsaṃjñaṃ namas tasmai vibhāvaso
yat tu tasmāt paraṃ rūpam om ity uktvābhisaṃhitam
asthūlaṃ sthūlam amalaṃ namas tasmai sanātana //
32.d:
विश्वम् एतत् त्रयीसंज्ञं नमस् तस्मै विभावसो
यत् तु तस्मात् परं रूपम् ओम् इत्य् उक्त्वाभिसंहितम्
अस्थूलं स्थूलम् अमलं नमस् तस्मै सनातन ॥
32.m:
This entire universe is known as the triad [of Vedas]; salutations to that form, O Vibhāvasu!
And salutations to that eternal form which is beyond that, unified by pronouncing 'Om',
subtle and gross, immaculate, O eternal one!

32.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ sā niyatā devī cakre stotram aharniśam
nirāhārā vivasvantam ārirādhayiṣur dvijāḥ //
32.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं सा नियता देवी चक्रे स्तोत्रम् अहर्निशम्
निराहारा विवस्वन्तम् आरिराधयिषुर् द्विजाः ॥
32.m:
Brahmā said:
Thus, O twice-born, that disciplined goddess, abstaining from food, offered praise day and night, wishing to propitiate Vivasvat.

32.s:
tataḥ kālena mahatā bhagavāṃs tapano dvijāḥ
pratyakṣatām agāt tasyā dākṣāyaṇyā dvijottamāḥ //
32.d:
ततः कालेन महता भगवांस् तपनो द्विजाः
प्रत्यक्षताम् अगात् तस्या दाक्षायण्या द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
32.m: Then after a long time, O twice-born, the lord, the burner, became visible to her, the daughter of Dakṣa, O best of twice-born.

32.s:
sā dadarśa mahākūṭaṃ tejaso 'mbarasaṃvṛtam
bhūmau ca saṃsthitaṃ bhāsvajjvālābhir atidurdṛśam
taṃ dṛṣṭvā ca tato devī sādhvasaṃ paramaṃ gatā //
32.d:
सा ददर्श महाकूटं तेजसो ऽम्बरसंवृतम्
भूमौ च संस्थितं भास्वज्ज्वालाभिर् अतिदुर्दृशम्
तं दृष्ट्वा च ततो देवी साध्वसं परमं गता ॥
32.m:
She saw a great peak of splendour covering the sky and resting upon the earth, very difficult to look upon with its blazing flames;
and seeing it, the goddess fell into great terror.

32.s:
aditir uvāca
jagadādya prasīdeti na tvāṃ paśyāmi gopate
prasādaṃ kuru paśyeyaṃ yad rūpaṃ te divākara
bhaktānukampaka vibho tvadbhaktān pāhi me sutān //
32.d:
अदितिर् उवाच
जगदाद्य प्रसीदेति न त्वां पश्यामि गोपते
प्रसादं कुरु पश्येयं यद् रूपं ते दिवाकर
भक्तानुकम्पक विभो त्वद्भक्तान् पाहि मे सुतान् ॥
32.m:
Aditi said:
Origin of the universe, be pleased! I do not see you, O lord of rays!
Grant favour so that I may see that form of yours, O sun!
O omnipresent one, compassionate to devotees, protect my sons who are devoted to you!

32.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ sa tejasas tasmād āvirbhūto vibhāvasuḥ
adṛśyata tadādityas taptatāmropamaḥ prabhuḥ //
32.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः स तेजसस् तस्माद् आविर्भूतो विभावसुः
अदृश्यत तदादित्यस् तप्तताम्रोपमः प्रभुः ॥

32.s:
tatas tāṃ praṇatāṃ devīṃ tasyāsaṃdarśane dvijāḥ
prāha bhāsvān vṛṇuṣvaikaṃ varaṃ matto yam icchasi //
32.d:
ततस् तां प्रणतां देवीं तस्यासंदर्शने द्विजाः
प्राह भास्वान् वृणुष्वैकं वरं मत्तो यम् इच्छसि ॥
32.m:
Then seeing her bowed, O twice-born, the radiant one spoke in her presence:
'Choose one boon from me, whatever you desire.'

32.s:
praṇatā śirasā sā tu jānupīḍitamedinī
pratyuvāca vivasvantaṃ varadaṃ samupasthitam //
32.d:
प्रणता शिरसा सा तु जानुपीडितमेदिनी
प्रत्युवाच विवस्वन्तं वरदं समुपस्थितम् ॥
32.m:
Prostrating with her head, her knees pressing the earth,
she replied to Vivasvat, the giver of boons, who stood before her.

32.s:
aditir uvāca
deva prasīda putrāṇāṃ hṛtaṃ tribhuvanaṃ mama
yajñabhāgāś ca daiteyair dānavaiś ca balādhikaiḥ //
32.d:
अदितिर् उवाच
देव प्रसीद पुत्राणां हृतं त्रिभुवनं मम
यज्ञभागाश् च दैतेयैर् दानवैश् च बलाधिकैः ॥
32.m:
Aditi said:
Be pleased, O god! The three worlds and the sacrificial shares of my sons
have been seized by the Daityas and Dānavas of superior strength.

32.s:
tannimittaṃ prasādaṃ tvaṃ kuruṣva mama gopate
aṃśena teṣāṃ bhrātṛtvaṃ gatvā tān nāśaye ripūn //
32.d:
तन्निमित्तं प्रसादं त्वं कुरुष्व मम गोपते
अंशेन तेषां भ्रातृत्वं गत्वा तान् नाशये रिपून् ॥
32.m:
Therefore, grant your favour to me, O lord of rays:
assuming brotherhood with them by a portion of yourself, destroy those enemies,

32.s:
yathā me tanayā bhūyo yajñabhāgabhujaḥ prabho
bhaveyur adhipāś caiva trailokyasya divākara //
32.d:
यथा मे तनया भूयो यज्ञभागभुजः प्रभो
भवेयुर् अधिपाश् चैव त्रैलोक्यस्य दिवाकर ॥
32.m:
so that my sons may once again be enjoyers of sacrificial shares, O lord,
and rulers of the three worlds, O sun!

32.s:
tathānukalpaṃ putrāṇāṃ suprasanno rave mama
kuru prasannārtihara kāryaṃ kartā tvam ucyate //
32.d:
तथानुकल्पं पुत्राणां सुप्रसन्नो रवे मम
कुरु प्रसन्नार्तिहर कार्यं कर्ता त्वम् उच्यते ॥
32.m:
Therefore, well-pleased, O sun, provide relief for my sons;
O dispeller of the distress of the pleased, you are declared to be the doer of what must be done!

32.s:
brahmovāca
tatas tām āha bhagavān bhāskaro vāritaskaraḥ
praṇatām aditiṃ viprāḥ prasādasumukho vibhuḥ //
32.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततस् ताम् आह भगवान् भास्करो वारितस्करः
प्रणताम् अदितिं विप्राः प्रसादसुमुखो विभुः ॥
32.m:
Brahmā said:
Then the lord, the maker of light, stealer of waters, the all-pervading one,
his face gracious with favour, spoke to the bowed Aditi, O brahmins.

32.s:
sūrya uvāca
sahasrāṃśena te garbhaḥ saṃbhūyāham aśeṣataḥ
tvatputraśatrūn dakṣo 'haṃ nāśayāmy āśu nirvṛtaḥ //
32.d:
सूर्य उवाच
सहस्रांशेन ते गर्भः संभूयाहम् अशेषतः
त्वत्पुत्रशत्रून् दक्षो ऽहं नाशयाम्य् आशु निर्वृतः ॥
32.m:
Sūrya said:
Having been conceived in your womb with a thousandth part, I, being capable, shall completely destroy the enemies of your sons, well-pleased, without delay.

32.s:
brahmovāca
ity uktvā bhagavān bhāsvān antardhānam upāgataḥ
nivṛttā sāpi tapasaḥ saṃprāptākhilavāñchitā //
32.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्य् उक्त्वा भगवान् भास्वान् अन्तर्धानम् उपागतः
निवृत्ता सापि तपसः संप्राप्ताखिलवाञ्छिता ॥

32.s:
tato raśmisahasrāt tu suṣumnākhyo raveḥ karaḥ
tataḥ saṃvatsarasyānte tatkāmapūraṇāya saḥ //
32.d:
ततो रश्मिसहस्रात् तु सुषुम्नाख्यो रवेः करः
ततः संवत्सरस्यान्ते तत्कामपूरणाय सः ॥
32.m:
Then, from the thousand rays, a ray of the sun named Suṣumnā [entered her];
then at the end of a year, in order to fulfill her desire,

32.s:
nivāsaṃ savitā cakre devamātus tadodare
kṛcchracāndrāyaṇādīṃś ca sā cakre susamāhitā //
32.d:
निवासं सविता चक्रे देवमातुस् तदोदरे
कृच्छ्रचान्द्रायणादींश् च सा चक्रे सुसमाहिता ॥
32.m:
Savity made his abode in the womb of the mother of the gods.
And she, deeply concentrated, observed kṛcchra, cāndrāyaṇa, and other austerities.

32.s:
śucinā dhārayāmy enaṃ divyaṃ garbham iti dvijāḥ
tatas tāṃ kaśyapaḥ prāha kiṃcitkopaplutākṣaram //
32.d:
शुचिना धारयाम्य् एनं दिव्यं गर्भम् इति द्विजाः
ततस् तां कश्यपः प्राह किंचित्कोपप्लुताक्षरम् ॥
32.m:
Saying, 'I shall bear this divine embryo in purity,' O twice-born;
then Kaśyapa said to her, his words slightly filled with anger:

32.s:
kaśyapa uvāca
kiṃ mārayasi garbhāṇḍam iti nityopavāsinī
sā ca taṃ prāha garbhāṇḍam etat paśyeti kopanā
na māritaṃ vipakṣāṇāṃ mṛtyur eva bhaviṣyati //
32.d:
कश्यप उवाच
किं मारयसि गर्भाण्डम् इति नित्योपवासिनी
सा च तं प्राह गर्भाण्डम् एतत् पश्येति कोपना
न मारितं विपक्षाणां मृत्युर् एव भविष्यति ॥
32.m:
Kaśyapa said:
'Why are you killing the egg of the womb by continually fasting?'
And she, angered, said to him: 'Look at this egg of the womb!
It is not killed; it will be the very death of our adversaries!'

32.s:
ity uktvā taṃ tadā garbham utsasarja surāraṇiḥ
jājvalyamānaṃ tejobhiḥ patyur vacanakopitā //
32.d:
इत्य् उक्त्वा तं तदा गर्भम् उत्ससर्ज सुरारणिः
जाज्वल्यमानं तेजोभिः पत्युर् वचनकोपिता ॥
32.m:
Having spoken thus, the fire-stick of the gods, angered by her husband's words,
then cast out that embryo blazing with splendours.

32.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā kaśyapo garbham udyadbhāskaravarcasam
tuṣṭāva praṇato bhūtvā vāgbhir ādyābhir ādarāt //
32.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा कश्यपो गर्भम् उद्यद्भास्करवर्चसम्
तुष्टाव प्रणतो भूत्वा वाग्भिर् आद्याभिर् आदरात् ॥
32.m:
Seeing that embryo possessing the lustre of the rising sun,
Kaśyapa bowed down and praised it with primordial words out of reverence.

32.s:
saṃstūyamānaḥ sa tadā garbhāṇḍāt prakaṭo 'bhavat
padmapattrasavarṇābhas tejasā vyāptadiṅmukhaḥ //
32.d:
संस्तूयमानः स तदा गर्भाण्डात् प्रकटो ऽभवत्
पद्मपत्त्रसवर्णाभस् तेजसा व्याप्तदिङ्मुखः ॥
32.m:
Being praised then, he became manifest from the egg of the womb,
with a complexion like a lotus petal, pervading the directions with splendour.

32.s:
athāntarikṣād ābhāṣya kaśyapaṃ munisattamam
satoyameghagambhīrā vāg uvācāśarīriṇī //
32.d:
अथान्तरिक्षाद् आभाष्य कश्यपं मुनिसत्तमम्
सतोयमेघगम्भीरा वाग् उवाचाशरीरिणी ॥
32.m:
Then, addressing Kaśyapa, best of sages, from the sky,
a bodiless voice spoke, deep as a rain-cloud:

32.s:
vāg uvāca
māritaṃtepataḥ proktam etad aṇḍaṃ tvayāditeḥ
tasmān mune sutas te 'yaṃ mārtaṇḍākhyo bhaviṣyati //
32.d:
वाग् उवाच
मारितंतेपतः प्रोक्तम् एतद् अण्डं त्वयादितेः
तस्मान् मुने सुतस् ते ऽयं मार्तण्डाख्यो भविष्यति ॥
32.m:
The voice said:
'Because this egg of Aditi was said by you to be killed,
therefore, O sage, this son of yours will be named Mārtaṇḍa.

32.s:
haniṣyaty asurāṃś cāyaṃ yajñabhāgaharān arīn
devā niśamyeti vaco gaganāt samupāgatam //
32.d:
हनिष्यत्य् असुरांश् चायं यज्ञभागहरान् अरीन्
देवा निशम्येति वचो गगनात् समुपागतम् ॥
32.m:
And he will slay the asuras, the enemies who steal the sacrificial shares.'
Having heard this speech that came from the sky, the gods [rejoiced]...

32.s:
praharṣam atulaṃ yātā dānavāś ca hataujasaḥ
tato yuddhāya daiteyān ājuhāva śatakratuḥ //
32.d:
प्रहर्षम् अतुलं याता दानवाश् च हतौजसः
ततो युद्धाय दैतेयान् आजुहाव शतक्रतुः ॥
32.m: The gods attained peerless joy, and the Dānavas lost their vigor. / Then Śatakratu challenged the sons of Diti to battle.

32.s:
saha devair mudā yukto dānavāś ca tam abhyayuḥ
teṣāṃ yuddham abhūd ghoraṃ devānām asuraiḥ saha //
32.d:
सह देवैर् मुदा युक्तो दानवाश् च तम् अभ्ययुः
तेषां युद्धम् अभूद् घोरं देवानाम् असुरैः सह ॥
32.m: Filled with joy, he advanced with the gods, and the Dānavas confronted him. / A dreadful battle took place between those gods and the asuras,

32.s:
śastrāstravṛṣṭisaṃdīptasamastabhuvanāntaram
tasmin yuddhe bhagavatā mārtaṇḍena nirīkṣitāḥ //
32.d:
शस्त्रास्त्रवृष्टिसंदीप्तसमस्तभुवनान्तरम्
तस्मिन् युद्धे भगवता मार्तण्डेन निरीक्षिताः ॥
32.m: with the whole interior of the world set ablaze by a shower of weapons and missiles. / Looked upon in that battle by the blessed Mārtaṇḍa,

32.s:
tejasā dahyamānās te bhasmībhūtā mahāsurāḥ
tataḥ praharṣam atulaṃ prāptāḥ sarve divaukasaḥ //
32.d:
तेजसा दह्यमानास् ते भस्मीभूता महासुराः
ततः प्रहर्षम् अतुलं प्राप्ताः सर्वे दिवौकसः ॥
32.m: those great asuras were burned by his splendor and turned to ashes. / Then all the dwellers of heaven attained peerless joy.

32.s:
tuṣṭuvus tejasāṃ yoniṃ mārtaṇḍam aditiṃ tathā
svādhikārāṃs tataḥ prāptā yajñabhāgāṃś ca pūrvavat //
32.d:
तुष्टुवुस् तेजसां योनिं मार्तण्डम् अदितिं तथा
स्वाधिकारांस् ततः प्राप्ता यज्ञभागांश् च पूर्ववत् ॥
32.m: They praised Mārtaṇḍa, the source of splendors, and likewise Aditi. / Then they attained their offices and their sacrificial shares as before.

32.s:
bhagavān api mārtaṇḍaḥ svādhikāram athākarot
kadambapuṣpavad bhāsvān adhaś cordhvaṃ ca raśmibhiḥ
vṛto 'gnipiṇḍasadṛśo dadhre nātisphuṭaṃ vapuḥ //
32.d:
भगवान् अपि मार्तण्डः स्वाधिकारम् अथाकरोत्
कदम्बपुष्पवद् भास्वान् अधश् चोर्ध्वं च रश्मिभिः
वृतो ऽग्निपिण्डसदृशो दध्रे नातिस्फुटं वपुः ॥
32.m: The blessed Mārtaṇḍa also assumed his office. / Like a kadamba flower, surrounded below and above by rays, / resembling a ball of fire, the sun bore a form that was not very distinct.

32.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
kathaṃ kāntataraṃ paścād rūpaṃ saṃlabdhavān raviḥ
kadambagolakākāraṃ tan me brūhi jagatpate //
32.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
कथं कान्ततरं पश्चाद् रूपं संलब्धवान् रविः
कदम्बगोलकाकारं तन् मे ब्रूहि जगत्पते ॥
32.m: The sages said: / How did the sun later obtain a lovelier form / instead of that spherical shape like a kadamba flower? Tell me that, O lord of the world!

32.s:
brahmovāca
tvaṣṭā tasmai dadau kanyāṃ saṃjñāṃ nāma vivasvate
prasādya praṇato bhūtvā viśvakarmā prajāpatiḥ //
32.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
त्वष्टा तस्मै ददौ कन्यां संज्ञां नाम विवस्वते
प्रसाद्य प्रणतो भूत्वा विश्वकर्मा प्रजापतिः ॥
32.m: Brahmā said: / Having propitiated him and bowed down, Tvaṣṭṛ, that is, the lord of creatures Viśvakarman, / gave to that Vivasvat his daughter named Saṃjñā.

32.s:
trīṇy apatyāny asau tasyāṃ janayām āsa gopatiḥ
dvau putrau sumahābhāgau kanyāṃ ca yamunāṃ tathā //
32.d:
त्रीण्य् अपत्यान्य् असौ तस्यां जनयाम् आस गोपतिः
द्वौ पुत्रौ सुमहाभागौ कन्यां च यमुनां तथा ॥
32.m: That lord of rays begot upon her three offspring: / two most fortunate sons, and likewise a daughter, Yamunā.

32.s:
yat tejo 'bhyadhikaṃ tasya mārtaṇḍasya vivasvataḥ
tenātitāpayām āsa trīṃl lokān sacarācarān //
32.d:
यत् तेजो ऽभ्यधिकं तस्य मार्तण्डस्य विवस्वतः
तेनातितापयाम् आस त्रींल् लोकान् सचराचरान् ॥
32.m: With the excessive splendor that belonged to that Mārtaṇḍa Vivasvat, / he intensely scorched the three worlds, together with all that moves and is still.

32.s:
tad rūpaṃ golakākāraṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjñā vivasvataḥ
asahantī mahat tejaḥ svāṃ chāyāṃ vākyam abravīt //
32.d:
तद् रूपं गोलकाकारं दृष्ट्वा संज्ञा विवस्वतः
असहन्ती महत् तेजः स्वां छायां वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥
32.m: Seeing that spherical form of Vivasvat, / Saṃjñā, unable to bear the great splendor, spoke these words to her Chāyā:

32.s:
saṃjñovāca
ahaṃ yāsyāmi bhadraṃ te svam eva bhavanaṃ pituḥ
nirvikāraṃ tvayātraiva stheyaṃ macchāsanāc chubhe //
32.d:
संज्ञोवाच
अहं यास्यामि भद्रं ते स्वम् एव भवनं पितुः
निर्विकारं त्वयात्रैव स्थेयं मच्छासनाच् छुभे ॥
32.m: Saṃjñā said: / May good betide you! I shall go to my father's own home. / By my command, O auspicious one, you must remain right here without altering your appearance.

32.s:
imau ca bālakau mahyaṃ kanyā ca varavarṇinī
saṃbhāvyā naiva cākhyeyam idaṃ bhagavate tvayā //
32.d:
इमौ च बालकौ मह्यं कन्या च वरवर्णिनी
संभाव्या नैव चाख्येयम् इदं भगवते त्वया ॥
32.m: And these two young boys of mine and the fair-complexioned daughter / are to be cherished, and this must never be told to the blessed lord by you.

32.s:
chāyovāca
ā kacagrahaṇād devi ā śāpān naiva karhicit
ākhyāsyāmi mataṃ tubhyaṃ gamyatāṃ yatra vāñchitam //
32.d:
छायोवाच
आ कचग्रहणाद् देवि आ शापान् नैव कर्हिचित्
आख्यास्यामि मतं तुभ्यं गम्यतां यत्र वाञ्छितम् ॥
32.m: Chāyā said: / O goddess, until I am seized by the hair, until a curse [is threatened], never / will I disclose your plan. Go wherever you wish!

32.s:
ity uktā vrīḍitā saṃjñā jagāma pitṛmandiram
vatsarāṇāṃ sahasraṃ tu vasamānā pitur gṛhe //
32.d:
इत्य् उक्ता व्रीडिता संज्ञा जगाम पितृमन्दिरम्
वत्सराणां सहस्रं तु वसमाना पितुर् गृहे ॥
32.m: Spoken to thus, the embarrassed Saṃjñā went to her father's dwelling. / And while she was living in her father's house for a thousand years,

32.s:
bhartuḥ samīpaṃ yāhīti pitroktā sā punaḥ punaḥ
āgacchad vaḍavā bhūtvā kurūn athottarāṃs tataḥ //
32.d:
भर्तुः समीपं याहीति पित्रोक्ता सा पुनः पुनः
आगच्छद् वडवा भूत्वा कुरून् अथोत्तरांस् ततः ॥
32.m: she was told again and again by her father, 'Go back to your husband!' / Thereupon, turning into a mare, she went to the Northern Kurus.

32.s:
tatra tepe tapaḥ sādhvī nirāhārā dvijottamāḥ
pituḥ samīpaṃ yātāyāṃ saṃjñāyāṃ vākyatatparā //
32.d:
तत्र तेपे तपः साध्वी निराहारा द्विजोत्तमाः
पितुः समीपं यातायां संज्ञायां वाक्यतत्परा ॥
32.m: There that virtuous woman, abstaining from food, practiced austerities, O best of the twice-born. / When Saṃjñā had gone to her father, [Chāyā,] devoted to her word,

32.s:
tadrūpadhāriṇī chāyā bhāskaraṃ samupasthitā
tasyāṃ ca bhagavān sūryaḥ saṃjñeyam iti cintayan //
32.d:
तद्रूपधारिणी छाया भास्करं समुपस्थिता
तस्यां च भगवान् सूर्यः संज्ञेयम् इति चिन्तयन् ॥
32.m: wearing her form, waited upon the sun. / And upon her the blessed Sūrya, thinking, 'This is Saṃjñā,'

32.s:
tathaiva janayām āsa dvau putrau kanyakāṃ tathā
saṃjñā tu pārthivī teṣām ātmajānāṃ tathākarot //
32.d:
तथैव जनयाम् आस द्वौ पुत्रौ कन्यकां तथा
संज्ञा तु पार्थिवी तेषाम् आत्मजानां तथाकरोत् ॥
32.m: likewise begot two sons and a daughter. / But that earthly Saṃjñā showed such [affection] toward her own children;

32.s:
snehaṃ na pūrvajātānāṃ tathā kṛtavatī tu sā
manus tat kṣāntavāṃs tasyā yamas tasyā na cakṣame //
32.d:
स्नेहं न पूर्वजातानां तथा कृतवती तु सा
मनुस् तत् क्षान्तवांस् तस्या यमस् तस्या न चक्षमे ॥
32.m: she did not, however, show the same affection toward the earlier-born. / Manu forgave her for that, but Yama did not pardon her.

32.s:
bahudhā pīḍyamānas tu pituḥ patyā suduḥkhitaḥ
sa vai kopāc ca bālyāc ca bhāvino 'rthasya vai balāt
padā saṃtarjayām āsa na tu dehe nyapātayat //
32.d:
बहुधा पीड्यमानस् तु पितुः पत्या सुदुःखितः
स वै कोपाच् च बाल्याच् च भाविनो ऽर्थस्य वै बलात्
पदा संतर्जयाम् आस न तु देहे न्यपातयत् ॥
32.m: Tormented in many ways by his father's wife, deeply aggrieved, / out of anger, childishness, and the force of inevitable destiny, / he threatened her with his foot, but did not bring it down upon her body.

32.s:
chāyovāca
padā tarjayase yasmāt pitur bhāryāṃ garīyasīm
tasmāt tavaiṣa caraṇaḥ patiṣyati na saṃśayaḥ //
32.d:
छायोवाच
पदा तर्जयसे यस्मात् पितुर् भार्यां गरीयसीम्
तस्मात् तवैष चरणः पतिष्यति न संशयः ॥
32.m: Chāyā said: / Since you threaten your father's senior wife with your foot, / therefore this foot of yours will fall off; there is no doubt!

32.s:
brahmovāca
yamas tu tena śāpena bhṛśaṃ pīḍitamānasaḥ
manunā saha dharmātmā pitre sarvaṃ nyavedayat //
32.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
यमस् तु तेन शापेन भृशं पीडितमानसः
मनुना सह धर्मात्मा पित्रे सर्वं न्यवेदयत् ॥
32.m: Brahmā said: / His mind severely tormented by that curse, / the righteous Yama reported everything to his father along with Manu.

32.s:
yama uvāca
snehena tulyam asmāsu mātā deva na vartate
visṛjya jyāyasaṃ bhaktyā kanīyāṃsaṃ bubhūṣati //
32.d:
यम उवाच
स्नेहेन तुल्यम् अस्मासु माता देव न वर्तते
विसृज्य ज्यायसं भक्त्या कनीयांसं बुभूषति ॥
32.m: Yama said: / O lord, our mother does not behave toward us with equal affection. / Neglecting the elder, she devotedly wishes to nurture the younger.

32.s:
tasyāṃ mayodyataḥ pādo na tu dehe nipātitaḥ
bālyād vā yadi vā mohāt tad bhavān kṣantum arhasi //
32.d:
तस्यां मयोद्यतः पादो न तु देहे निपातितः
बाल्याद् वा यदि वा मोहात् तद् भवान् क्षन्तुम् अर्हसि ॥
32.m: My foot was raised toward her, but it was not brought down upon her body. / Whether out of childishness or delusion, you ought to forgive that.

32.s:
śapto 'haṃ tāta kopena jananyā tanayo yataḥ
tato manye na jananīm imāṃ vai tapatāṃ vara //
32.d:
शप्तो ऽहं तात कोपेन जनन्या तनयो यतः
ततो मन्ये न जननीम् इमां वै तपतां वर ॥
32.m: Father, since I, her son, was cursed in anger by my mother, / therefore, O best of the radiant, I do not believe she is my mother!

32.s:
tava prasādāc caraṇo bhagavan na pated yathā
mātṛśāpād ayaṃ me 'dya tathā cintaya gopate //
32.d:
तव प्रसादाच् चरणो भगवन् न पतेद् यथा
मातृशापाद् अयं मे ऽद्य तथा चिन्तय गोपते ॥
32.m: O blessed lord, devise a means by your grace so that my foot / may not fall off today due to my mother's curse, O lord of rays!

32.s:
ravir uvāca
asaṃśayaṃ mahat putra bhaviṣyaty atra kāraṇam
yena tvām āviśat krodho dharmajñaṃ dharmaśīlinam //
32.d:
रविर् उवाच
असंशयं महत् पुत्र भविष्यत्य् अत्र कारणम्
येन त्वाम् आविशत् क्रोधो धर्मज्ञं धर्मशीलिनम् ॥
32.m: Ravi said: / Undoubtedly, my son, there must be a great reason here / why anger entered you, who know dharma and practice dharma.

32.s:
sarveṣām eva śāpānāṃ pratighāto hi vidyate
na tu mātrābhiśaptānāṃ kvacic chāpanivartanam //
32.d:
सर्वेषाम् एव शापानां प्रतिघातो हि विद्यते
न तु मात्राभिशप्तानां क्वचिच् छापनिवर्तनम् ॥
32.m: Indeed, for all curses a counteraction is found, / but for those cursed by a mother there is nowhere any revocation of the curse.

32.s:
na śakyam etan mithyā tu kartuṃ mātur vacas tava
kiṃcit te 'haṃ vidhāsyāmi putrasnehād anugraham //
32.d:
न शक्यम् एतन् मिथ्या तु कर्तुं मातुर् वचस् तव
किंचित् ते ऽहं विधास्यामि पुत्रस्नेहाद् अनुग्रहम् ॥
32.m: It is not possible to make this word of your mother false. / Out of love for my son, I shall grant you a slight favor.

32.s:
kṛmayo māṃsam ādāya prayāsyanti mahītalam
kṛtaṃ tasyā vacaḥ satyaṃ tvaṃ ca trāto bhaviṣyasi //
32.d:
कृमयो मांसम् आदाय प्रयास्यन्ति महीतलम्
कृतं तस्या वचः सत्यं त्वं च त्रातो भविष्यसि ॥
32.m: Worms will take flesh [from it] and go to the surface of the earth. / Her word will thus be made true, and you will be saved.

32.s:
brahmovāca
ādityas tv abravīc chāyāṃ kimarthaṃ tanayeṣu vai
tulyeṣv apy adhikaḥ sneha ekaṃ prati kṛtas tvayā //
32.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
आदित्यस् त्व् अब्रवीच् छायां किमर्थं तनयेषु वै
तुल्येष्व् अप्य् अधिकः स्नेह एकं प्रति कृतस् त्वया ॥
32.m: Brahmā said: / Āditya then said to Chāyā: 'Why, among sons / who are equal, have you shown greater affection toward one [group]?

32.s:
nūnaṃ naiṣāṃ tvaṃ jananī saṃjñā kāpi tvam āgatā
nirguṇeṣv apy apatyeṣu mātā śāpaṃ na dāsyati //
32.d:
नूनं नैषां त्वं जननी संज्ञा कापि त्वम् आगता
निर्गुणेष्व् अप्य् अपत्येषु माता शापं न दास्यति ॥
32.m: Surely you are not their mother Saṃjñā; you are some stranger who has come! / Even toward sons devoid of virtue, a mother does not give a curse.'

32.s:
sā tatpariharantī ca śāpād bhītā tadā raveḥ
kathayām āsa vṛttāntaṃ sa śrutvā śvaśuraṃ yayau //
32.d:
सा तत्परिहरन्ती च शापाद् भीता तदा रवेः
कथयाम् आस वृत्तान्तं स श्रुत्वा श्वशुरं ययौ ॥
32.m: Failing to evade [his questioning] and terrified of Ravi's curse, / she related the whole account. Hearing that, he went to his father-in-law.

32.s:
sa cāpi taṃ yathānyāyam arcayitvā tadā ravim
nirdagdhukāmaṃ roṣeṇa sāntvayānas tam abravīt //
32.d:
स चापि तं यथान्यायम् अर्चयित्वा तदा रविम्
निर्दग्धुकामं रोषेण सान्त्वयानस् तम् अब्रवीत् ॥
32.m: Having duly worshipped Ravi at that time, / [Viśvakarman,] consoling him who wished to burn [everything] in his fury, said to him:

32.s:
viśvakarmovāca
tavātitejasā vyāptam idaṃ rūpaṃ suduḥsaham
asahantī tu tat saṃjñā vane carati vai tapaḥ //
32.d:
विश्वकर्मोवाच
तवातितेजसा व्याप्तम् इदं रूपं सुदुःसहम्
असहन्ती तु तत् संज्ञा वने चरति वै तपः ॥
32.m: Viśvakarman said: / Pervaded by your excessive splendor, this form of yours is very difficult to endure. / Unable to bear it, Saṃjñā is indeed performing austerities in the forest.

32.s:
drakṣyate tāṃ bhavān adya svāṃ bhāryāṃ śubhacāriṇīm
rūpārthaṃ bhavato 'raṇye carantīṃ sumahat tapaḥ //
32.d:
द्रक्ष्यते तां भवान् अद्य स्वां भार्यां शुभचारिणीम्
रूपार्थं भवतो ऽरण्ये चरन्तीं सुमहत् तपः ॥
32.m: You will see her today, your wife of auspicious conduct, / performing immense austerities in the wilderness for the sake of your [pleasing] form.

32.s:
śrutaṃ me brahmaṇo vākyaṃ tava tejovarodhane
rūpaṃ nirvartayāmy adya tava kāntaṃ divaspate //
32.d:
श्रुतं मे ब्रह्मणो वाक्यं तव तेजोवरोधने
रूपं निर्वर्तयाम्य् अद्य तव कान्तं दिवस्पते ॥
32.m: I have heard Brahmā's word regarding the curtailment of your splendor. / Today, O lord of heaven, I shall fashion a lovely form for you.

32.s:
brahmovāca
tatas tatheti taṃ prāha tvaṣṭāraṃ bhagavān raviḥ
tato vivasvato rūpaṃ prāg āsīt parimaṇḍalam //
32.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततस् तथेति तं प्राह त्वष्टारं भगवान् रविः
ततो विवस्वतो रूपं प्राग् आसीत् परिमण्डलम् ॥
32.m: Brahmā said: / Then the blessed Ravi said 'So be it' to Tvaṣṭṛ. / Formerly the form of Vivasvat was entirely circular.

32.s:
viśvakarmā tv anujñātaḥ śākadvīpe vivasvatā
bhramim āropya tattejaḥśātanāyopacakrame //
32.d:
विश्वकर्मा त्व् अनुज्ञातः शाकद्वीपे विवस्वता
भ्रमिम् आरोप्य तत्तेजःशातनायोपचक्रमे ॥
32.m: Permitted by Vivasvat, Viśvakarman placed him upon a lathe / in Śākadvīpa and set about paring down his splendor.

32.s:
bhramatāśeṣajagatāṃ nābhibhūtena bhāsvatā
samudrādrivanopetā tv āruroha mahī nabhaḥ //
32.d:
भ्रमताशेषजगतां नाभिभूतेन भास्वता
समुद्राद्रिवनोपेता त्व् आरुरोह मही नभः ॥
32.m: As the sun, who is the nave of all the worlds, revolved, / the earth, endowed with oceans, mountains, and forests, rose into the sky.

32.s:
gaganaṃ cākhilaṃ viprāḥ sacandragrahatārakam
adhogataṃ mahābhāgā babhūvākṣiptam ākulam //
32.d:
गगनं चाखिलं विप्राः सचन्द्रग्रहतारकम्
अधोगतं महाभागा बभूवाक्षिप्तम् आकुलम् ॥
32.m: And the entire firmament, O twice-born sages, with its moon, planets, and stars, / turned downward, tossed about and agitated, O fortunate ones!

32.s:
vikṣiptasalilāḥ sarve babhūvuś ca tathārṇavāḥ
vyabhidyanta mahāśailāḥ śīrṇasānunibandhanāḥ //
32.d:
विक्षिप्तसलिलाः सर्वे बभूवुश् च तथार्णवाः
व्यभिद्यन्त महाशैलाः शीर्णसानुनिबन्धनाः ॥
32.m: All the oceans had their waters hurled about, / and great mountains were split apart, their mountain-peak bonds shattered.

32.s:
dhruvādhārāṇy aśeṣāṇi dhiṣṇyāni munisattamāḥ
truṭyadraśminibandhīni bandhanāni adho yayuḥ //
32.d:
ध्रुवाधाराण्य् अशेषाणि धिष्ण्यानि मुनिसत्तमाः
त्रुट्यद्रश्मिनिबन्धीनि बन्धनानि अधो ययुः ॥
32.m: All the heavenly bodies resting on Dhruva, O best of sages, / with their ray-fastenings snapped, went tumbling downward.

32.s:
vegabhramaṇasaṃpātavāyukṣiptāḥ sahasraśaḥ
vyaśīryanta mahāmeghā ghorārāvavirāviṇaḥ //
32.d:
वेगभ्रमणसंपातवायुक्षिप्ताः सहस्रशः
व्यशीर्यन्त महामेघा घोरारावविराविणः ॥
32.m: Hurled by the thousands by the wind produced by the velocity of his spinning, / the great clouds, roaring with terrible sounds, broke apart.

32.s:
bhāsvadbhramaṇavibhrāntabhūmyākāśarasātalam
jagad ākulam atyarthaṃ tadāsīn munisattamāḥ //
32.d:
भास्वद्भ्रमणविभ्रान्तभूम्याकाशरसातलम्
जगद् आकुलम् अत्यर्थं तदासीन् मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
32.m: The earth, the sky, and the netherworld whirled around by the spinning of the sun; / the world became utterly confounded then, O best of sages.

32.s:
trailokyam ākulaṃ vīkṣya bhramamāṇaṃ surarṣayaḥ
devāś ca brahmaṇā sārdhaṃ bhāsvantam abhituṣṭuvuḥ //
32.d:
त्रैलोक्यम् आकुलं वीक्ष्य भ्रममाणं सुरर्षयः
देवाश् च ब्रह्मणा सार्धं भास्वन्तम् अभितुष्टुवुः ॥
32.m: Seeing the three worlds agitated and spinning, the divine sages / and the gods, together with Brahmā, praised the sun:

32.s:
ādidevo 'si devānāṃ jātas tvaṃ bhūtaye bhuvaḥ
sargasthityantakāleṣu tridhā bhedena tiṣṭhasi //
32.d:
आदिदेवो ऽसि देवानां जातस् त्वं भूतये भुवः
सर्गस्थित्यन्तकालेषु त्रिधा भेदेन तिष्ठसि ॥
32.m: “You are the primal god of gods; you were born for the welfare of the world. / At the times of creation, preservation, and end, you abide in a three-fold division.

32.s:
svasti te 'stu jagannātha gharmavarṣadivākara
indrādayas tadā devā likhyamānam athāstuvan //
32.d:
स्वस्ति ते ऽस्तु जगन्नाथ घर्मवर्षदिवाकर
इन्द्रादयस् तदा देवा लिख्यमानम् अथास्तुवन् ॥
32.m: May there be well-being unto you, Lord of the Universe, creator of day with heat and rain!” / Then Indra and the other gods praised [him] as he was being trimmed.

32.s:
jaya deva jagatsvāmiñ jayāśeṣajagatpate
ṛṣayaś ca tataḥ sapta vasiṣṭhātripurogamāḥ //
32.d:
जय देव जगत्स्वामिञ् जयाशेषजगत्पते
ऋषयश् च ततः सप्त वसिष्ठात्रिपुरोगमाः ॥
32.m: “Hail, O god, master of the universe! Hail, lord of the entire universe!” / Then the seven sages, headed by Vasiṣṭha and Atri,

32.s:
tuṣṭuvur vividhaiḥ stotraiḥ svasti svastītivādinaḥ
vedoktibhir athāgryābhir vālakhilyāś ca tuṣṭuvuḥ //
32.d:
तुष्टुवुर् विविधैः स्तोत्रैः स्वस्ति स्वस्तीतिवादिनः
वेदोक्तिभिर् अथाग्र्याभिर् वालखिल्याश् च तुष्टुवुः ॥
32.m: praised him with diverse hymns, crying, “Hail, hail!” / And the Vālakhilyas praised [him] with the foremost Vedic utterances.

32.s:
agnir ādyāś ca bhāsvantaṃ likhyamānaṃ mudā yutāḥ
tvaṃ nātha mokṣiṇāṃ mokṣo dhyeyas tvaṃ dhyānināṃ paraḥ //
32.d:
अग्निर् आद्याश् च भास्वन्तं लिख्यमानं मुदा युताः
त्वं नाथ मोक्षिणां मोक्षो ध्येयस् त्वं ध्यानिनां परः ॥
32.m: Agni and the others, full of joy, praised the sun as he was being pared: / “You, O Lord, are liberation for seekers of liberation; you are the supreme object of meditation for the meditative.

32.s:
tvaṃ gatiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ karmakāṇḍavivartinām
saṃpūjyas tvaṃ tu deveśa śaṃ no 'stu jagatāṃ pate //
32.d:
त्वं गतिः सर्वभूतानां कर्मकाण्डविवर्तिनाम्
संपूज्यस् त्वं तु देवेश शं नो ऽस्तु जगतां पते ॥
32.m: You are the refuge of all beings who engage in the ritual section of the Veda; / you are worthy of worship, O lord of gods! May there be peace for us, O lord of worlds!

32.s:
śaṃ no 'stu dvipade nityaṃ śaṃ naś cāstu catuṣpade
tato vidyādharagaṇā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ //
32.d:
शं नो ऽस्तु द्विपदे नित्यं शं नश् चास्तु चतुष्पदे
ततो विद्याधरगणा यक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः ॥
32.m: May there be peace for our two-footed creatures always, and peace for our four-footed!” / Then the hosts of Vidyādharas, the Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Pannagas,

32.s:
kṛtāñjalipuṭāḥ sarve śirobhiḥ praṇatā ravim
ūcus te vividhā vāco manaḥśrotrasukhāvahāḥ //
32.d:
कृताञ्जलिपुटाः सर्वे शिरोभिः प्रणता रविम्
ऊचुस् ते विविधा वाचो मनःश्रोत्रसुखावहाः ॥
32.m: all with hands joined in reverence, bowed with their heads to the sun, / and spoke diverse words bringing pleasure to the mind and ears:

32.s:
sahyaṃ bhavatu tejas te bhūtānāṃ bhūtabhāvana
tato hāhāhūhūś caiva nāradas tumburus tathā //
32.d:
सह्यं भवतु तेजस् ते भूतानां भूतभावन
ततो हाहाहूहूश् चैव नारदस् तुम्बुरुस् तथा ॥
32.m: “May your brilliance become bearable for beings, O creator of beings!” / Then Hāhā and Hūhū, and Nārada and Tumburu,

32.s:
upagāyitum ārabdhā gāndharvakuśalā ravim
ṣaḍjamadhyamagāndhāragānatrayaviśāradāḥ //
32.d:
उपगायितुम् आरब्धा गान्धर्वकुशला रविम्
षड्जमध्यमगान्धारगानत्रयविशारदाः ॥
32.m: skilled in the art of the Gandharvas, began to sing to the sun, / expert in the three styles of singing: ṣaḍja, madhyama, and gāndhāra,

32.s:
mūrchanābhiś ca tālaiś ca saṃprayogaiḥ sukhapradam
viśvācī ca ghṛtācī ca urvaśy atha tilottamāḥ //
32.d:
मूर्छनाभिश् च तालैश् च संप्रयोगैः सुखप्रदम्
विश्वाची च घृताची च उर्वश्य् अथ तिलोत्तमाः ॥
32.m: delightful with melodic modulations, rhythms, and musical combinations. / Viśvācī, Ghṛtācī, Urvaśī, and Tilottamā,

32.s:
menakā sahajanyā ca rambhā cāpsarasāṃ varā
nanṛtur jagatām īśe likhyamāne vibhāvasau //
32.d:
मेनका सहजन्या च रम्भा चाप्सरसां वरा
ननृतुर् जगताम् ईशे लिख्यमाने विभावसौ ॥
32.m: Menakā, Sahajanyā, and Rambhā, the foremost of the Apsarases, / danced while the sun, the lord of worlds, was being pared,

32.s:
bhāvahāvavilāsādyān kurvatyo 'bhinayān bahūn
prāvādyanta tatas tatra vīṇā veṇvādijharjharāḥ //
32.d:
भावहावविलासाद्यान् कुर्वत्यो ऽभिनयान् बहून्
प्रावाद्यन्त ततस् तत्र वीणा वेण्वादिझर्झराः ॥
32.m: displaying many theatrical gestures beginning with emotional states, gestures, and dalliance. / Then there were sounded the lute, the flute, and other percussion instruments,

32.s:
paṇavāḥ puṣkarāś caiva mṛdaṅgāḥ paṭahānakāḥ
devadundubhayaḥ śaṅkhāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ //
32.d:
पणवाः पुष्कराश् चैव मृदङ्गाः पटहानकाः
देवदुन्दुभयः शङ्खाः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
32.m: small drums, pushkara drums, clay drums, kettle-drums and tabors, / celestial drums, and conches by hundreds and by thousands.

32.s:
gāyadbhiś caiva nṛtyadbhir gandharvair apsarogaṇaiḥ
tūryavāditraghoṣaiś ca sarvaṃ kolāhalīkṛtam //
32.d:
गायद्भिश् चैव नृत्यद्भिर् गन्धर्वैर् अप्सरोगणैः
तूर्यवादित्रघोषैश् च सर्वं कोलाहलीकृतम् ॥
32.m: With the singing and dancing of the Gandharvas and hosts of Apsarases, / and with the sounds of musical instruments, everything was filled with a loud commotion.

32.s:
tataḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭā bhaktinamrātmamūrtayaḥ
likhyamānaṃ sahasrāṃśuṃ praṇemuḥ sarvadevatāḥ //
32.d:
ततः कृताञ्जलिपुटा भक्तिनम्रात्ममूर्तयः
लिख्यमानं सहस्रांशुं प्रणेमुः सर्वदेवताः ॥
32.m: Then with hands joined in reverence, their bodies bowed in devotion, / all the deities bowed down to the thousand-rayed sun as he was being trimmed.

32.s:
tataḥ kolāhale tasmin sarvadevasamāgame
tejasaḥ śātanaṃ cakre viśvakarmā śanaiḥ śanaiḥ //
32.d:
ततः कोलाहले तस्मिन् सर्वदेवसमागमे
तेजसः शातनं चक्रे विश्वकर्मा शनैः शनैः ॥
32.m: Then, amid that uproar, at that assembly of all the gods, / Viśvakarman slowly pared down his brilliance.

32.s:
ājānulikhitaś cāsau nipuṇaṃ viśvakarmaṇā
nābhyanandat tu likhanaṃ tatas tenāvatāritaḥ //
32.d:
आजानुलिखितश् चासौ निपुणं विश्वकर्मणा
नाभ्यनन्दत् तु लिखनं ततस् तेनावतारितः ॥
32.m: When he had been trimmed down to his knees skillfully by Viśvakarman, / he did not approve of the trimming; therefore he was lowered down by him.

32.s:
na tu nirbhartsitaṃ rūpaṃ tejaso hananena tu
kāntāt kāntataraṃ rūpam adhikaṃ śuśubhe tataḥ //
32.d:
न तु निर्भर्त्सितं रूपं तेजसो हननेन तु
कान्तात् कान्ततरं रूपम् अधिकं शुशुभे ततः ॥
32.m: His beauty was by no means marred by the reduction of his brilliance; / his form shone all the more, far more lovely than lovely.

32.s:
iti himajalagharmakālahetor
harakamalāsanaviṣṇusaṃstutasya
tadupari likhanaṃ niśamya bhānor
vrajati divākaralokam āyuṣo 'nte
32.d:
इति हिमजलघर्मकालहेतोर्
हरकमलासनविष्णुसंस्तुतस्य
तदुपरि लिखनं निशम्य भानोर्
व्रजति दिवाकरलोकम् आयुषो ऽन्ते
32.m: Hearing of this paring done upon the sun, the cause of the seasons of cold, rain, and heat, / who was praised by Śiva, Brahmā, and Viṣṇu, / one goes to the world of the sun at the end of life.

32.s:
evaṃ janma raveḥ pūrvaṃ babhūva munisattamāḥ
rūpaṃ ca paramaṃ tasya mayā saṃparikīrtitam //
32.d:
एवं जन्म रवेः पूर्वं बभूव मुनिसत्तमाः
रूपं च परमं तस्य मया संपरिकीर्तितम् ॥
32.m: Thus the birth of the sun took place in ancient times, O best of sages, / and his supreme form has been described by me.

33.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
bhūyo 'pi kathayāsmākaṃ kathāṃ sūryasamāśritām
na tṛptim adhigacchāmaḥ śṛṇvantas tāṃ kathāṃ śubhām //
33.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
भूयो ऽपि कथयास्माकं कथां सूर्यसमाश्रिताम्
न तृप्तिम् अधिगच्छामः शृण्वन्तस् तां कथां शुभाम् ॥
33.m: The sages said: / “Tell us again the narrative concerning the sun; / we are not satisfied as we listen to that auspicious tale.

33.s:
yo 'yaṃ dīpto mahātejā vahnirāśisamaprabhaḥ
etad veditum icchāmaḥ prabhāvo 'sya kutaḥ prabho //
33.d:
यो ऽयं दीप्तो महातेजा वह्निराशिसमप्रभः
एतद् वेदितुम् इच्छामः प्रभावो ऽस्य कुतः प्रभो ॥
33.m: This blazing one of immense brilliance, who shines like a heap of fire— / we wish to know this, O lord: whence comes his majesty?”

33.s:
brahmovāca
tamobhūteṣu lokeṣu naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame
prakṛter guṇahetus tu pūrvaṃ buddhir ajāyata //
33.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तमोभूतेषु लोकेषु नष्टे स्थावरजङ्गमे
प्रकृतेर् गुणहेतुस् तु पूर्वं बुद्धिर् अजायत ॥
33.m: Brahmā said: / “When the worlds had become darkness, when stationary and moving beings were destroyed, / first from the primal nature, as the cause of the qualities, intellect arose.

33.s:
ahaṃkāras tato jāto mahābhūtapravartakaḥ
vāyvagnir āpaḥ khaṃ bhūmis tatas tv aṇḍam ajāyata //
33.d:
अहंकारस् ततो जातो महाभूतप्रवर्तकः
वाय्वग्निर् आपः खं भूमिस् ततस् त्व् अण्डम् अजायत ॥
33.m: From that arose the ego-principle, which brings forth the gross elements: / wind, fire, waters, ether, and earth; then the egg arose.

33.s:
tasminn aṇḍe tv ime lokāḥ sapta caiva pratiṣṭhitāḥ
pṛthivī saptabhir dvīpaiḥ samudraiś caiva saptabhiḥ //
33.d:
तस्मिन्न् अण्डे त्व् इमे लोकाः सप्त चैव प्रतिष्ठिताः
पृथिवी सप्तभिर् द्वीपैः समुद्रैश् चैव सप्तभिः ॥
33.m: In that egg these seven worlds are established, / and the earth with its seven continents and seven oceans.

33.s:
tatraivāvasthito hy āsīd ahaṃ viṣṇur maheśvaraḥ
vimūḍhās tāmasāḥ sarve pradhyāyanti tam īśvaram //
33.d:
तत्रैवावस्थितो ह्य् आसीद् अहं विष्णुर् महेश्वरः
विमूढास् तामसाः सर्वे प्रध्यायन्ति तम् ईश्वरम् ॥
33.m: I, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara were stationed right there. / All the deluded beings, shrouded in darkness, meditated upon that Lord.

33.s:
tato vai sumahātejāḥ prādurbhūtas tamonudaḥ
dhyānayogena cāsmābhir vijñātaḥ savitā tadā //
33.d:
ततो वै सुमहातेजाः प्रादुर्भूतस् तमोनुदः
ध्यानयोगेन चास्माभिर् विज्ञातः सविता तदा ॥
33.m: Then indeed the dispeller of darkness, of immense splendor, became manifest; / and by the yoga of meditation, Savitṛ was then recognized by us.

33.s:
jñātvā ca paramātmānaṃ sarva eva pṛthak pṛthak
divyābhiḥ stutibhir devaḥ stuto 'smābhis tadeśvaraḥ //
33.d:
ज्ञात्वा च परमात्मानं सर्व एव पृथक् पृथक्
दिव्याभिः स्तुतिभिर् देवः स्तुतो ऽस्माभिस् तदेश्वरः ॥
33.m: And having recognized the supreme self, each and every one of us / praised that god, the Lord, with divine hymns:

33.s:
ādidevo 'si devānām aiśvaryāc ca tvam īśvaraḥ
ādikartāsi bhūtānāṃ devadevo divākaraḥ //
33.d:
आदिदेवो ऽसि देवानाम् ऐश्वर्याच् च त्वम् ईश्वरः
आदिकर्तासि भूतानां देवदेवो दिवाकरः ॥
33.m: ‘You are the primal god among gods, and through sovereignty you are the Lord; / you are the original maker of beings, the god of gods, the sun,

33.s:
jīvanaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ devagandharvarakṣasām
munikiṃnarasiddhānāṃ tathaivoragapakṣiṇām //
33.d:
जीवनः सर्वभूतानां देवगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्
मुनिकिंनरसिद्धानां तथैवोरगपक्षिणाम् ॥
33.m: the life of all beings, of gods, Gandharvas, and Rakṣases, / of sages, Kinnaras, and Siddhas, and likewise of serpents and birds.

33.s:
tvaṃ brahmā tvaṃ mahādevas tvaṃ viṣṇus tvaṃ prajāpatiḥ
vāyur indraś ca somaś ca vivasvān varuṇas tathā //
33.d:
त्वं ब्रह्मा त्वं महादेवस् त्वं विष्णुस् त्वं प्रजापतिः
वायुर् इन्द्रश् च सोमश् च विवस्वान् वरुणस् तथा ॥
33.m: You are Brahmā, you are Mahādeva, you are Viṣṇu, you are Prajāpati; / you are Vāyu, Indra, Soma, Vivasvat, and Varuṇa.

33.s:
tvaṃ kālaḥ sṛṣṭikartā ca hartā bhartā tathā prabhuḥ
saritaḥ sāgarāḥ śailā vidyudindradhanūṃṣi ca //
33.d:
त्वं कालः सृष्टिकर्ता च हर्ता भर्ता तथा प्रभुः
सरितः सागराः शैला विद्युदिन्द्रधनूंषि च ॥
33.m: You are Time, the creator, the destroyer, the sustainer, and the lord, / the rivers, the oceans, the mountains, and lightning and rainbows,

33.s:
pralayaḥ prabhavaś caiva vyaktāvyaktaḥ sanātanaḥ
īśvarāt parato vidyā vidyāyāḥ parataḥ śivaḥ //
33.d:
प्रलयः प्रभवश् चैव व्यक्ताव्यक्तः सनातनः
ईश्वरात् परतो विद्या विद्यायाः परतः शिवः ॥
33.m: dissolution and origin, manifest and unmanifest, eternal. / Beyond the lord is wisdom; beyond wisdom is Śiva;

33.s:
śivāt parataro devas tvam eva parameśvaraḥ
sarvataḥpāṇipādāntaḥ sarvatokṣiśiromukhaḥ //
33.d:
शिवात् परतरो देवस् त्वम् एव परमेश्वरः
सर्वतःपाणिपादान्तः सर्वतोक्षिशिरोमुखः ॥
33.m: higher than Śiva is the god, you yourself, the supreme lord, / whose hands and feet are everywhere, whose eyes, heads, and faces are everywhere,

33.s:
sahasrāṃśuḥ sahasrāsyaḥ sahasracaraṇekṣaṇaḥ
bhūtādir bhūr bhuvaḥ svaś ca mahaḥ satyaṃ tapo janaḥ //
33.d:
सहस्रांशुः सहस्रास्यः सहस्रचरणेक्षणः
भूतादिर् भूर् भुवः स्वश् च महः सत्यं तपो जनः ॥
33.m: the thousand-rayed, thousand-faced, with a thousand feet and eyes, / source of beings, Bhūr, Bhuvas, Svar, Mahas, Satya, Tapas, and Janas.

33.s:
pradīptaṃ dīpanaṃ divyaṃ sarvalokaprakāśakam
durnirīkṣaṃ surendrāṇāṃ yad rūpaṃ tasya te namaḥ //
33.d:
प्रदीप्तं दीपनं दिव्यं सर्वलोकप्रकाशकम्
दुर्निरीक्षं सुरेन्द्राणां यद् रूपं तस्य ते नमः ॥
33.m: Blazing, illuminating, divine, illuminating all worlds, / difficult to behold even for the lords of gods: homage to that form of yours!

33.s:
surasiddhagaṇair juṣṭaṃ bhṛgvatripulahādibhiḥ
stutaṃ paramam avyaktaṃ yad rūpaṃ tasya te namaḥ //
33.d:
सुरसिद्धगणैर् जुष्टं भृग्वत्रिपुलहादिभिः
स्तुतं परमम् अव्यक्तं यद् रूपं तस्य ते नमः ॥
33.m: Resorted to by hosts of gods and Siddhas, praised by Bhṛgu, Atri, Pulaha, and others, / supreme and unmanifest: homage to that form of yours!

33.s:
vedyaṃ vedavidāṃ nityaṃ sarvajñānasamanvitam
sarvadevātidevasya yad rūpaṃ tasya te namaḥ //
33.d:
वेद्यं वेदविदां नित्यं सर्वज्ञानसमन्वितम्
सर्वदेवातिदेवस्य यद् रूपं तस्य ते नमः ॥
33.m: Constantly to be known by knowers of the Veda, endowed with all knowledge, / belonging to the supreme deity among all gods: homage to that form of yours!

33.s:
viśvakṛd viśvabhūtaṃ ca vaiśvānarasurārcitam
viśvasthitam acintyaṃ ca yad rūpaṃ tasya te namaḥ //
33.d:
विश्वकृद् विश्वभूतं च वैश्वानरसुरार्चितम्
विश्वस्थितम् अचिन्त्यं च यद् रूपं तस्य ते नमः ॥
33.m: The maker of all, identical with the universe, worshipped by fire and gods, / abiding in the universe, and inconceivable: homage to that form of yours!

33.s:
paraṃ yajñāt paraṃ vedāt paraṃ lokāt paraṃ divaḥ
paramātmety abhikhyātaṃ yad rūpaṃ tasya te namaḥ //
33.d:
परं यज्ञात् परं वेदात् परं लोकात् परं दिवः
परमात्मेत्य् अभिख्यातं यद् रूपं तस्य ते नमः ॥
33.m: Higher than sacrifice, higher than the Veda, higher than the world, higher than heaven, / known as the supreme self: homage to that form of yours!

33.s:
avijñeyam anālakṣyam adhyānagatam avyayam
anādinidhanaṃ caiva yad rūpaṃ tasya te namaḥ //
33.d:
अविज्ञेयम् अनालक्ष्यम् अध्यानगतम् अव्ययम्
अनादिनिधनं चैव यद् रूपं तस्य ते नमः ॥
33.m: Unknowable, unperceivable, beyond the reach of meditation, imperishable, / and without beginning or end: homage to that form of yours!

33.s:
namo namaḥ kāraṇakāraṇāya
namo namaḥ pāpavimocanāya
namo namas te ditijārdanāya
namo namo rogavimocanāya
33.d:
नमो नमः कारणकारणाय
नमो नमः पापविमोचनाय
नमो नमस् ते दितिजार्दनाय
नमो नमो रोगविमोचनाय
33.m: Homage, homage to the cause of causes! / Homage, homage to the deliverer from sins! / Homage, homage to you, the tormentor of the sons of Diti! / Homage, homage to the deliverer from diseases!

33.s:
namo namaḥ sarvavarapradāya
namo namaḥ sarvasukhapradāya
namo namaḥ sarvadhanapradāya
namo namaḥ sarvamatipradāya
33.d:
नमो नमः सर्ववरप्रदाय
नमो नमः सर्वसुखप्रदाय
नमो नमः सर्वधनप्रदाय
नमो नमः सर्वमतिप्रदाय
33.m: Homage, homage to the granter of all boons! / Homage, homage to the giver of all happiness! / Homage, homage to the granter of all wealth! / Homage, homage to the giver of all intelligence!’”

33.s:
stutaḥ sa bhagavān evaṃ taijasaṃ rūpam āsthitaḥ
uvāca vācā kalyāṇyā ko varo vaḥ pradīyatām //
33.d:
स्तुतः स भगवान् एवं तैजसं रूपम् आस्थितः
उवाच वाचा कल्याण्या को वरो वः प्रदीयताम् ॥
33.m: Praised thus, the Blessed One, abiding in a fiery form, / spoke with an auspicious voice: 'Which boon should be granted to you?'

33.s:
devā ūcuḥ
tavātitaijasaṃ rūpaṃ na kaścit soḍhum utsahet
sahanīyaṃ tad bhavatu hitāya jagataḥ prabho //
33.d:
देवा ऊचुः
तवातितैजसं रूपं न कश्चित् सोढुम् उत्सहेत्
सहनीयं तद् भवतु हिताय जगतः प्रभो ॥
33.m: The gods said: / 'No one could endure your excessively fiery form; / let it become bearable, O Lord, for the welfare of the world.'

33.s:
evam astv iti so 'py uktvā bhagavān ādikṛt prabhuḥ
lokānāṃ kāryasiddhyarthaṃ gharmavarṣahimapradaḥ //
33.d:
एवम् अस्त्व् इति सो ऽप्य् उक्त्वा भगवान् आदिकृत् प्रभुः
लोकानां कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थं घर्मवर्षहिमप्रदः ॥
33.m: Having said, 'So be it,' that Blessed Lord, the primal creator, / bestowing heat, rain, and cold for the accomplishment of the worlds' tasks,

33.s:
tataḥ sāṃkhyāś ca yogāś ca ye cānye mokṣakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
dhyāyanti dhyāyino devaṃ hṛdayasthaṃ divākaram //
33.d:
ततः सांख्याश् च योगाश् च ये चान्ये मोक्षकाङ्क्षिणः
ध्यायन्ति ध्यायिनो देवं हृदयस्थं दिवाकरम् ॥
33.m: thenceforth the Sāṃkhyas and yogins, and whatever others long for liberation, / as meditators meditate upon the god, the Sun, residing in the heart.

33.s:
sarvalakṣaṇahīno 'pi yukto vā sarvapātakaiḥ
sarvaṃ ca tarate pāpaṃ devam arkaṃ samāśritaḥ //
33.d:
सर्वलक्षणहीनो ऽपि युक्तो वा सर्वपातकैः
सर्वं च तरते पापं देवम् अर्कं समाश्रितः ॥
33.m: Even if devoid of all auspicious marks, or tainted by all sins, / having taken refuge in the god Arka, one crosses over every sin.

33.s:
agnihotraṃ ca vedāś ca yajñāś ca bahudakṣiṇāḥ
bhānor bhaktinamaskārakalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm //
33.d:
अग्निहोत्रं च वेदाश् च यज्ञाश् च बहुदक्षिणाः
भानोर् भक्तिनमस्कारकलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम् ॥
33.m: The Agnihotra, the Vedas, and sacrifices with abundant priestly gifts / are not worth a sixteenth part of devotion and salutation to the Sun.

33.s:
tīrthānāṃ paramaṃ tīrthaṃ maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam
pavitraṃ ca pavitrāṇāṃ prapadyante divākaram //
33.d:
तीर्थानां परमं तीर्थं मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम्
पवित्रं च पवित्राणां प्रपद्यन्ते दिवाकरम् ॥
33.m: The supreme sacred ford of all sacred fords, the most auspicious of all auspicious things, / and the purest of all pure things: they take refuge in the Sun.

33.s:
śakrādyaiḥ saṃstutaṃ devaṃ ye namasyanti bhāskaram
sarvakilbiṣanirmuktāḥ sūryalokaṃ vrajanti te //
33.d:
शक्राद्यैः संस्तुतं देवं ये नमस्यन्ति भास्करम्
सर्वकिल्बिषनिर्मुक्ताः सूर्यलोकं व्रजन्ति ते ॥
33.m: Those who bow to the god Bhāskara, who is praised by Indra and others, / freed from all sins, go to the world of the Sun.

33.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
cirāt prabhṛti no brahmañ śrotum icchā pravartate
nāmnām aṣṭaśataṃ brūhi yat tvayoktaṃ purā raveḥ //
33.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
चिरात् प्रभृति नो ब्रह्मञ् श्रोतुम् इच्छा प्रवर्तते
नाम्नाम् अष्टशतं ब्रूहि यत् त्वयोक्तं पुरा रवेः ॥
33.m: The sages said: / 'For a long time, O Brahmā, a desire has arisen in us to hear. / Tell us the one hundred and eight names of the Sun that were spoken by you long ago.'

33.s:
brahmovāca
aṣṭottaraśataṃ nāmnāṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ gadato mama
bhāskarasya paraṃ guhyaṃ svargamokṣapradaṃ dvijāḥ //
33.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
अष्टोत्तरशतं नाम्नां शृणुध्वं गदतो मम
भास्करस्य परं गुह्यं स्वर्गमोक्षप्रदं द्विजाः ॥
33.m: Brahmā said: / 'Listen, O twice-born, as I declare the one hundred and eight names / of Bhāskara, the supreme secret that grants heaven and liberation:

33.s:
oṃ sūryo 'ryamā bhagas tvaṣṭā pūṣārkaḥ savitā raviḥ
gabhastimān ajaḥ kālo mṛtyur dhātā prabhākaraḥ //
33.d:
ओं सूर्यो ऽर्यमा भगस् त्वष्टा पूषार्कः सविता रविः
गभस्तिमान् अजः कालो मृत्युर् धाता प्रभाकरः ॥
33.m: Oṃ. Sūrya, Aryaman, Bhaga, Tvaṣṭṛ, Pūṣan, Arka, Savitṛ, Ravi, / Gabhastimat, Aja, Kāla, Mṛtyu, Dhātṛ, Prabhākara,

33.s:
pṛthivy āpaś ca tejaś ca khaṃ vāyuś ca parāyaṇam
somo bṛhaspatiḥ śukro budho 'ṅgāraka eva ca //
33.d:
पृथिव्य् आपश् च तेजश् च खं वायुश् च परायणम्
सोमो बृहस्पतिः शुक्रो बुधो ऽङ्गारक एव च ॥
33.m: Earth, Water, Fire, Sky, and Wind, the Supreme Goal, / Soma, Bṛhaspati, Śukra, Budha, and Aṅgāraka,

33.s:
indro vivasvān dīptāṃśuḥ śuciḥ śauriḥ śanaiścaraḥ
brahmā viṣṇuś ca rudraś ca skando vaiśravaṇo yamaḥ //
33.d:
इन्द्रो विवस्वान् दीप्तांशुः शुचिः शौरिः शनैश्चरः
ब्रह्मा विष्णुश् च रुद्रश् च स्कन्दो वैश्रवणो यमः ॥
33.m: Indra, Vivasvat, Dīptāṃśu, Śuci, Śauri, Śanaiścara, / Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Skanda, Vaiśravaṇa, Yama,

33.s:
vaidyuto jāṭharaś cāgnir aindhanas tejasāṃ patiḥ
dharmadhvajo vedakartā vedāṅgo vedavāhanaḥ //
33.d:
वैद्युतो जाठरश् चाग्निर् ऐन्धनस् तेजसां पतिः
धर्मध्वजो वेदकर्ता वेदाङ्गो वेदवाहनः ॥
33.m: the Lightning-fire, the Digestive fire, the Fuel-born fire, the Lord of lights, / Dharmadhvaja, the Maker of the Vedas, Vedāṅga, Vedavāhana,

33.s:
kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaś ca kaliḥ sarvāmarāśrayaḥ
kalākāṣṭhāmuhūrtāś ca kṣapā yāmās tathā kṣaṇāḥ //
33.d:
कृतं त्रेता द्वापरश् च कलिः सर्वामराश्रयः
कलाकाष्ठामुहूर्ताश् च क्षपा यामास् तथा क्षणाः ॥
33.m: Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara, and Kali, the Abode of all immortals, / kalās, kāṣṭhās, muhūrtas, nights, watches, and moments,

33.s:
saṃvatsarakaro 'śvatthaḥ kālacakro vibhāvasuḥ
puruṣaḥ śāśvato yogī vyaktāvyaktaḥ sanātanaḥ //
33.d:
संवत्सरकरो ऽश्वत्थः कालचक्रो विभावसुः
पुरुषः शाश्वतो योगी व्यक्ताव्यक्तः सनातनः ॥
33.m: the Maker of the year, Aśvattha, the Wheel of Time, Vibhāvasu, / the Eternal Puruṣa, the Yogin, the Manifest and Unmanifest, the Primeval,

33.s:
kālādhyakṣaḥ prajādhyakṣo viśvakarmā tamonudaḥ
varuṇaḥ sāgaro 'ṃśaś ca jīmūto jivano 'rihā //
33.d:
कालाध्यक्षः प्रजाध्यक्षो विश्वकर्मा तमोनुदः
वरुणः सागरो ऽंशश् च जीमूतो जिवनो ऽरिहा ॥
33.m: the Overseer of Time, the Overseer of Creatures, Viśvakarman, the Dispeller of darkness, / Varuṇa, the Ocean, Aṃśa, the Cloud, the Giver of life, the Destroyer of enemies,

33.s:
bhūtāśrayo bhūtapatiḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ
sraṣṭā saṃvartako vahniḥ sarvasyādir alolupaḥ //
33.d:
भूताश्रयो भूतपतिः सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः
स्रष्टा संवर्तको वह्निः सर्वस्यादिर् अलोलुपः ॥
33.m: the Refuge of beings, the Lord of beings, the One saluted by all worlds, / the Creator, the Dissolver, Fire, the Origin of all, the Uncovetous,

33.s:
anantaḥ kapilo bhānuḥ kāmadaḥ sarvatomukhaḥ
jayo viśālo varadaḥ sarvabhūtaniṣevitaḥ //
33.d:
अनन्तः कपिलो भानुः कामदः सर्वतोमुखः
जयो विशालो वरदः सर्वभूतनिषेवितः ॥
33.m: the Endless, Kapila, the Sun, the Bestower of desires, the All-faced, / Victory, the Vast, the Boon-giver, served by all beings,

33.s:
manaḥ suparṇo bhūtādiḥ śīghragaḥ prāṇadhāraṇaḥ
dhanvantarir dhūmaketur ādidevo 'diteḥ sutaḥ //
33.d:
मनः सुपर्णो भूतादिः शीघ्रगः प्राणधारणः
धन्वन्तरिर् धूमकेतुर् आदिदेवो ऽदितेः सुतः ॥
33.m: the Mind, Suparṇa, the Source of beings, the Swift-moving, the Sustainer of life, / Dhanvantari, Dhūmaketu, the Primal God, the Son of Aditi,

33.s:
dvādaśātmā ravir dakṣaḥ pitā mātā pitāmahaḥ
svargadvāraṃ prajādvāraṃ mokṣadvāraṃ triviṣṭapam //
33.d:
द्वादशात्मा रविर् दक्षः पिता माता पितामहः
स्वर्गद्वारं प्रजाद्वारं मोक्षद्वारं त्रिविष्टपम् ॥
33.m: the Twelve-fold Self, Ravi, Dakṣa, the Father, the Mother, the Grandfather, / the Door to Heaven, the Door to Creatures, the Door to Liberation, Heaven,

33.s:
dehakartā praśāntātmā viśvātmā viśvatomukhaḥ
carācarātmā sūkṣmātmā maitreyaḥ karuṇānvitaḥ //
33.d:
देहकर्ता प्रशान्तात्मा विश्वात्मा विश्वतोमुखः
चराचरात्मा सूक्ष्मात्मा मैत्रेयः करुणान्वितः ॥
33.m: the Maker of the body, the Serene Self, the Self of the Universe, the All-faced, / the Self of the moving and unmoving, the Subtle Self, the Benevolent, full of compassion.'

33.s:
etad vai kīrtanīyasya sūryasyāmitatejasaḥ
nāmnām aṣṭaśataṃ ramyaṃ mayā proktaṃ dvijottamāḥ //
33.d:
एतद् वै कीर्तनीयस्य सूर्यस्यामिततेजसः
नाम्नाम् अष्टशतं रम्यं मया प्रोक्तं द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
33.m: Indeed, this charming [hymn of] one hundred and eight names of the Sun of boundless splendor, / who is worthy of praise, has been spoken by me, O best of the twice-born.

33.s:
suragaṇapitṛyakṣasevitaṃ hy
asuraniśākarasiddhavanditam
varakanakahutāśanaprabhaṃ
praṇipatito 'smi hitāya bhāskaram
33.d:
सुरगणपितृयक्षसेवितं ह्य्
असुरनिशाकरसिद्धवन्दितम्
वरकनकहुताशनप्रभं
प्रणिपतितो ऽस्मि हिताय भास्करम्
33.m: Served by the hosts of gods, ancestors, and yakṣas, / and praised by asuras, the moon, and siddhas, / having the radiance of fine gold and fire, / I bow down to the Sun for [our] welfare.

33.s:
sūryodaye yaḥ susamāhitaḥ paṭhet
sa putradārān dhanaratnasaṃcayān
labheta jātismaratāṃ naraḥ sa tu
smṛtiṃ ca medhāṃ ca sa vindate parām
33.d:
सूर्योदये यः सुसमाहितः पठेत्
स पुत्रदारान् धनरत्नसंचयान्
लभेत जातिस्मरतां नरः स तु
स्मृतिं च मेधां च स विन्दते पराम्
33.m: Whoever recites [this] with a concentrated mind at sunrise, / that person obtains sons, wives, and heaps of wealth and jewels; / he indeed obtains the memory of previous births, / and attains supreme memory and intelligence.

33.s:
imaṃ stavaṃ devavarasya yo naraḥ
prakīrtayec chuddhamanāḥ samāhitaḥ
vimucyate śokadavāgnisāgarāl
labheta kāmān manasā yathepsitān
33.d:
इमं स्तवं देववरस्य यो नरः
प्रकीर्तयेच् छुद्धमनाः समाहितः
विमुच्यते शोकदवाग्निसागराल्
लभेत कामान् मनसा यथेप्सितान्
33.m: The person who, with a purified mind and concentrated attention, / proclaims this praise of the best of gods, / is freed from the ocean of the forest fire of grief / and obtains the desires wished for in his heart.

34.s:
brahmovāca
yo 'sau sarvagato devas tripurāris trilocanaḥ
umāpriyakaro rudraś candrārdhakṛtaśekharaḥ //
34.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
यो ऽसौ सर्वगतो देवस् त्रिपुरारिस् त्रिलोचनः
उमाप्रियकरो रुद्रश् चन्द्रार्धकृतशेखरः ॥
34.m: Brahmā said: / 'That omnipresent god, the enemy of Tripura, the three-eyed, / who acts dear to Umā, Rudra, whose crest is the half-moon,

34.s:
vidrāvya vibudhān sarvān siddhavidyādharān ṛṣīn
gandharvayakṣanāgāṃś ca tathānyāṃś ca samāgatān //
34.d:
विद्राव्य विबुधान् सर्वान् सिद्धविद्याधरान् ऋषीन्
गन्धर्वयक्षनागांश् च तथान्यांश् च समागतान् ॥
34.m: having routed all the gods, siddhas, vidyādharas, and sages, / the gandharvas, yakṣas, nāgas, and the others who had gathered,

34.s:
jaghāna pūrvaṃ dakṣasya yajato dharaṇītale
yajñaṃ samṛddhaṃ ratnāḍhyaṃ sarvasaṃbhārasaṃbhṛtam //
34.d:
जघान पूर्वं दक्षस्य यजतो धरणीतले
यज्ञं समृद्धं रत्नाढ्यं सर्वसंभारसंभृतम् ॥
34.m: formerly destroyed the sacrifice of Dakṣa, who was sacrificing on the earth's surface— / [a sacrifice] abundant, rich with jewels, and equipped with all provisions—

34.s:
yasya pratāpasaṃtrastāḥ śakrādyās tridivaukasaḥ
śāntiṃ na lebhire viprāḥ kailāsaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ //
34.d:
यस्य प्रतापसंत्रस्ताः शक्राद्यास् त्रिदिवौकसः
शान्तिं न लेभिरे विप्राः कैलासं शरणं गताः ॥
34.m: terrified by whose blazing power, Indra and the other denizens of heaven / found no peace, O Brahmins, and went to Kailāsa for refuge.

34.s:
sa āste tatra varadaḥ śūlapāṇir vṛṣadhvajaḥ
pinākapāṇir bhagavān dakṣayajñavināśanaḥ //
34.d:
स आस्ते तत्र वरदः शूलपाणिर् वृषध्वजः
पिनाकपाणिर् भगवान् दक्षयज्ञविनाशनः ॥
34.m: He sits there, the boon-giver, trident in hand, whose emblem is the bull, / with the Pināka bow in hand, the Blessed One, the destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice,

34.s:
mahādevo 'kale deśe kṛttivāsā vṛṣadhvajaḥ
ekāmrake muniśreṣṭhāḥ sarvakāmaprado haraḥ //
34.d:
महादेवो ऽकले देशे कृत्तिवासा वृषध्वजः
एकाम्रके मुनिश्रेष्ठाः सर्वकामप्रदो हरः ॥
34.m: the Great God in an unblemished region, clad in animal skin, whose emblem is the bull, / Hara, who bestows all desires, in Ekāmraka, O best of sages.'

34.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
kimarthaṃ sa bhavo devaḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ
jaghāna yajñaṃ dakṣasya devaiḥ sarvair alaṃkṛtam //
34.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
किमर्थं स भवो देवः सर्वभूतहिते रतः
जघान यज्ञं दक्षस्य देवैः सर्वैर् अलंकृतम् ॥
34.m: The sages said: / 'For what reason did that god Bhava, who is devoted to the welfare of all beings, / destroy the sacrifice of Dakṣa, which was adorned by all the gods?

34.s:
na hy alpaṃ kāraṇaṃ tatra prabho manyāmahe vayam
śrotum icchāmahe brūhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ //
34.d:
न ह्य् अल्पं कारणं तत्र प्रभो मन्यामहे वयम्
श्रोतुम् इच्छामहे ब्रूहि परं कौतूहलं हि नः ॥
34.m: Indeed, we consider that the reason there was not small, O Lord; / we wish to hear; tell us, for our curiosity is immense.'

34.s:
brahmovāca
dakṣasyāsann aṣṭa kanyā yāś caivaṃ patisaṃgatāḥ
svebhyo gṛhebhyaś cānīya tāḥ pitābhyarcayad gṛhe //
34.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
दक्षस्यासन्न् अष्ट कन्या याश् चैवं पतिसंगताः
स्वेभ्यो गृहेभ्यश् चानीय ताः पिताभ्यर्चयद् गृहे ॥
34.m: Brahmā said: / 'Dakṣa had eight daughters who had thus been given to husbands; / having brought them from their homes, the father honored them in his house.

34.s:
tatas tv abhyarcitā viprā nyavasaṃs tāḥ pitur gṛhe
tāsāṃ jyeṣṭhā satī nāma patnī yā tryambakasya vai //
34.d:
ततस् त्व् अभ्यर्चिता विप्रा न्यवसंस् ताः पितुर् गृहे
तासां ज्येष्ठा सती नाम पत्नी या त्र्यम्बकस्य वै ॥
34.m: Then, having been honored, O Brahmins, they dwelt in their father's house. / The eldest of them was named Satī, the wife of Tryambaka.

34.s:
nājuhāvātmajāṃ tāṃ vai dakṣo rudram abhidviṣan
akarot saṃnatiṃ dakṣe na ca kāṃcin maheśvaraḥ //
34.d:
नाजुहावात्मजां तां वै दक्षो रुद्रम् अभिद्विषन्
अकरोत् संनतिं दक्षे न च कांचिन् महेश्वरः ॥
34.m: Dakṣa, bearing hatred toward Rudra, did not invite that daughter of his. / Nor did Maheśvara make any bow to Dakṣa.

34.s:
jāmātā śvaśure tasmin svabhāvāt tejasi sthitaḥ
tato jñātvā satī sarvās tās tu prāptāḥ pitur gṛham //
34.d:
जामाता श्वशुरे तस्मिन् स्वभावात् तेजसि स्थितः
ततो ज्ञात्वा सती सर्वास् तास् तु प्राप्ताः पितुर् गृहम् ॥
34.m: The son-in-law remained in his inherent splendor before that father-in-law. / Then, knowing that all of them had arrived at their father's house,

34.s:
jagāma sāpy anāhūtā satī tu svapitur gṛham
tābhyo hīnāṃ pitā cakre satyāḥ pūjām asaṃmatām
tato 'bravīt sā pitaraṃ devī krodhasamākulā //
34.d:
जगाम साप्य् अनाहूता सती तु स्वपितुर् गृहम्
ताभ्यो हीनां पिता चक्रे सत्याः पूजाम् असंमताम्
ततो ऽब्रवीत् सा पितरं देवी क्रोधसमाकुला ॥
34.m: Satī also went, uninvited, to her own father's house. / The father showed Satī a lesser and disrespectful reception compared to them; / then the goddess, agitated with anger, spoke to her father.'

34.s:
saty uvāca
yavīyasībhyaḥ śreṣṭhāhaṃ kiṃ na pūjasi māṃ prabho
asatkṛtām avasthāṃ yaḥ kṛtavān asi garhitām
ahaṃ jyeṣṭhā variṣṭhā ca māṃ tvaṃ satkartum arhasi //
34.d:
सत्य् उवाच
यवीयसीभ्यः श्रेष्ठाहं किं न पूजसि मां प्रभो
असत्कृताम् अवस्थां यः कृतवान् असि गर्हिताम्
अहं ज्येष्ठा वरिष्ठा च मां त्वं सत्कर्तुम् अर्हसि ॥
34.m: Satī said: / 'I am superior to the younger ones; why do you not honor me, O Lord? / You who have placed [me] in an unhonored, blameworthy condition— / I am the eldest and the most excellent, and you ought to treat me with honor.'

34.s:
brahmovāca
evam ukto 'bravīd enāṃ dakṣaḥ saṃraktalocanaḥ //
34.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवम् उक्तो ऽब्रवीद् एनां दक्षः संरक्तलोचनः ॥
34.m: Brahmā said: / 'Addressed in this way, Dakṣa, with bloodshot eyes, spoke to her.'

34.s:
dakṣa uvāca
tvattaḥ śreṣṭhā variṣṭhāś ca pūjyā bālāḥ sutā mama
tāsāṃ ye caiva bhartāras te me bahumatāḥ sati //
34.d:
दक्ष उवाच
त्वत्तः श्रेष्ठा वरिष्ठाश् च पूज्या बालाः सुता मम
तासां ये चैव भर्तारस् ते मे बहुमताः सति ॥
34.m: Dakṣa said: / 'My younger daughters are superior and more excellent than you, and worthy of honor. / And their husbands are highly regarded by me, O Satī.

34.s:
brahmiṣṭhāś ca vratasthāś ca mahāyogāḥ sudhārmikāḥ
guṇaiś caivādhikāḥ ślāghyāḥ sarve te tryambakāt sati //
34.d:
ब्रह्मिष्ठाश् च व्रतस्थाश् च महायोगाः सुधार्मिकाः
गुणैश् चैवाधिकाः श्लाघ्याः सर्वे ते त्र्यम्बकात् सति ॥
34.m: Devoted to sacred study, steadfast in vows, of great yogic power, and very virtuous, / all of them are superior in virtues and praiseworthy compared to Tryambaka, O Satī.

34.s:
vasiṣṭho 'triḥ pulastyaś ca aṅgirāḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ
bhṛgur marīciś ca tathā śreṣṭhā jāmātaro mama //
34.d:
वसिष्ठो ऽत्रिः पुलस्त्यश् च अङ्गिराः पुलहः क्रतुः
भृगुर् मरीचिश् च तथा श्रेष्ठा जामातरो मम ॥
34.m: Vasiṣṭha, Atri, Pulastya, Aṅgiras, Pulaha, Kratu, / Bhṛgu, and Marīci are my excellent sons-in-law.'

34.s:
taiś cāpi spardhate śarvaḥ sarve te caiva taṃ prati
tena tvāṃ na bubhūṣāmi pratikūlo hi me bhavaḥ //
34.d:
तैश् चापि स्पर्धते शर्वः सर्वे ते चैव तं प्रति
तेन त्वां न बुभूषामि प्रतिकूलो हि मे भवः ॥
34.m: And Śarva competes with them, and all of them against him. / Therefore I do not wish to have you; for Bhava is opposed to me.

34.s:
ity uktavāṃs tadā dakṣaḥ saṃpramūḍhena cetasā
śāpārtham ātmanaś caiva yenoktā vai maharṣayaḥ
tathoktā pitaraṃ sā vai kruddhā devī tam abravīt //
34.d:
इत्य् उक्तवांस् तदा दक्षः संप्रमूढेन चेतसा
शापार्थम् आत्मनश् चैव येनोक्ता वै महर्षयः
तथोक्ता पितरं सा वै क्रुद्धा देवी तम् अब्रवीत् ॥
34.m: Dakṣa having spoken thus at that time with a deluded mind, / by which he spoke to the great sages so as to bring a curse upon himself, / thus addressed, the enraged goddess said to her father:

34.s:
saty uvāca
vāṅmanaḥkarmabhir yasmād aduṣṭāṃ māṃ vigarhasi
tasmāt tyajāmy ahaṃ deham imaṃ tāta tavātmajam //
34.d:
सत्य् उवाच
वाङ्मनःकर्मभिर् यस्माद् अदुष्टां मां विगर्हसि
तस्मात् त्यजाम्य् अहं देहम् इमं तात तवात्मजम् ॥
34.m: Satī said: / Since you revile me, faultless in speech, mind, and deeds, / therefore, father, I abandon this body born of you.

34.s:
brahmovāca
tatas tenāpamānena satī duḥkhād amarṣitā
abravīd vacanaṃ devī namaskṛtya svayaṃbhuve //
34.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततस् तेनापमानेन सती दुःखाद् अमर्षिता
अब्रवीद् वचनं देवी नमस्कृत्य स्वयंभुवे ॥
34.m: Brahmā said: / Then, incensed with grief at that insult, / the goddess, having bowed to Svayambhū, spoke these words:

34.s:
saty uvāca
yenāham apadehā vai punar dehena bhāsvatā
tatrāpy aham asaṃmūḍhā saṃbhūtā dhārmikī punaḥ
gaccheyaṃ dharmapatnītvaṃ tryambakasyaiva dhīmataḥ //
34.d:
सत्य् उवाच
येनाहम् अपदेहा वै पुनर् देहेन भास्वता
तत्राप्य् अहम् असंमूढा संभूता धार्मिकी पुनः
गच्छेयं धर्मपत्नीत्वं त्र्यम्बकस्यैव धीमतः ॥
34.m: Satī said: / In so far as I am now bodiless, having arisen again with a resplendent body, / unbewildered even there, righteous once more, / may I attain the status of lawful wife to the wise Tryambaka alone.

34.s:
brahmovāca
tatraivātha samāsīnā ruṣṭātmānaṃ samādadhe
dhārayām āsa cāgneyīṃ dhāraṇām ātmanātmani //
34.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तत्रैवाथ समासीना रुष्टात्मानं समादधे
धारयाम् आस चाग्नेयीं धारणाम् आत्मनात्मनि ॥
34.m: Brahmā said: / Seated right there, enraged, she concentrated her mind; / by herself she maintained the fiery concentration within herself.

34.s:
tataḥ svātmānam utthāpya vāyunā samudīritaḥ
sarvāṅgebhyo viniḥsṛtya vahnir bhasma cakāra tām //
34.d:
ततः स्वात्मानम् उत्थाप्य वायुना समुदीरितः
सर्वाङ्गेभ्यो विनिःसृत्य वह्निर् भस्म चकार ताम् ॥
34.m: Then, having aroused her self, stimulated by the wind, / the fire, bursting forth from all her limbs, reduced her to ashes.

34.s:
tad upaśrutya nidhanaṃ satyā devyāḥ sa śūladhṛk
saṃvādaṃ ca tayor buddhvā yāthātathyena śaṃkaraḥ
dakṣasya ca vināśāya cukopa bhagavān prabhuḥ //
34.d:
तद् उपश्रुत्य निधनं सत्या देव्याः स शूलधृक्
संवादं च तयोर् बुद्ध्वा याथातथ्येन शंकरः
दक्षस्य च विनाशाय चुकोप भगवान् प्रभुः ॥
34.m: Hearing of that demise of the goddess Satī, that bearer of the trident, / Śaṅkara, understanding truly the dialogue of the two, / the blessed lord became enraged for the destruction of Dakṣa.

34.s:
śrīśaṃkara uvāca
yasmād avamatā dakṣa sahasaivāgatā satī
praśastāś cetarāḥ sarvās tvatsutā bhartṛbhiḥ saha //
34.d:
श्रीशंकर उवाच
यस्माद् अवमता दक्ष सहसैवागता सती
प्रशस्ताश् चेतराः सर्वास् त्वत्सुता भर्तृभिः सह ॥
34.m: Śrī Śaṅkara said: / Because Satī, who came here at once, was insulted, O Dakṣa, / while all your other daughters together with their husbands were praised,

34.s:
tasmād vaivasvate prāpte punar ete maharṣayaḥ
utpatsyanti dvitīye vai tava yajñe hy ayonijāḥ //
34.d:
तस्माद् वैवस्वते प्राप्ते पुनर् एते महर्षयः
उत्पत्स्यन्ति द्वितीये वै तव यज्ञे ह्य् अयोनिजाः ॥
34.m: therefore, when the Vaivasvata [manvantara] arrives, these great sages / will be born again, not from a womb, at your second sacrifice.

34.s:
hute vai brahmaṇaḥ sattre cākṣuṣasyāntare manoḥ
abhivyāhṛtya saptarṣīn dakṣaṃ so 'bhyaśapat punaḥ //
34.d:
हुते वै ब्रह्मणः सत्त्रे चाक्षुषस्यान्तरे मनोः
अभिव्याहृत्य सप्तर्षीन् दक्षं सो ऽभ्यशपत् पुनः ॥
34.m: When the sacrificial session of Brahmā has been offered in the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara, / having addressed the seven sages, he cursed Dakṣa again:

34.s:
bhavitā mānuṣo rājā cākṣuṣasyāntare manoḥ
prācīnabarhiṣaḥ pautraḥ putraś cāpi pracetasaḥ //
34.d:
भविता मानुषो राजा चाक्षुषस्यान्तरे मनोः
प्राचीनबर्हिषः पौत्रः पुत्रश् चापि प्रचेतसः ॥
34.m: “You will be a mortal king in the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara, / the grandson of Prācīnabarhis and the son of the Pracetas.

34.s:
dakṣa ity eva nāmnā tvaṃ māriṣāyāṃ janiṣyasi
kanyāyāṃ śākhināṃ caiva prāpte vai cākṣuṣāntare //
34.d:
दक्ष इत्य् एव नाम्ना त्वं मारिषायां जनिष्यसि
कन्यायां शाखिनां चैव प्राप्ते वै चाक्षुषान्तरे ॥
34.m: By the very name of Dakṣa you will be born of Māriṣā, / the daughter of the trees, when the Cākṣuṣa period has arrived.

34.s:
ahaṃ tatrāpi te vighnam ācariṣyāmi durmate
dharmakāmārthayukteṣu karmasv iha punaḥ punaḥ //
34.d:
अहं तत्रापि ते विघ्नम् आचरिष्यामि दुर्मते
धर्मकामार्थयुक्तेषु कर्मस्व् इह पुनः पुनः ॥
34.m: There too, evil-minded one, I will cause obstacles / repeatedly to your deeds connected with dharma, desire, and worldly wealth here.”

34.s: tato vai vyāhṛto dakṣo rudraṃ so 'bhyaśapat punaḥ //
34.d: ततो वै व्याहृतो दक्षो रुद्रं सो ऽभ्यशपत् पुनः ॥
34.m: Then, being thus reviled, Dakṣa cursed Rudra in return:

34.s:
dakṣa uvāca
yasmāt tvaṃ matkṛte krūra ṛṣīn vyāhṛtavān asi
tasmāt sārdhaṃ surair yajñe na tvāṃ yakṣyanti vai dvijāḥ //
34.d:
दक्ष उवाच
यस्मात् त्वं मत्कृते क्रूर ऋषीन् व्याहृतवान् असि
तस्मात् सार्धं सुरैर् यज्ञे न त्वां यक्ष्यन्ति वै द्विजाः ॥
34.m: Dakṣa said: / “Because you, cruel one, have reviled the sages on my account, / therefore the twice-born will not worship you together with the gods in the sacrifice.

34.s:
kṛtvāhutiṃ tava krūra apaḥ spṛśanti karmasu
ihaiva vatsyase loke divaṃ hitvāyugakṣayāt
tato devais tu te sārdhaṃ na tu pūjā bhaviṣyati //
34.d:
कृत्वाहुतिं तव क्रूर अपः स्पृशन्ति कर्मसु
इहैव वत्स्यसे लोके दिवं हित्वायुगक्षयात्
ततो देवैस् तु ते सार्धं न तु पूजा भविष्यति ॥
34.m: Having made an oblation to you, cruel one, they will touch water in the rituals. / Leaving heaven, you will dwell right here in this world until the end of the yuga, / and there will be no worship for you along with the gods.”

34.s:
rudra uvāca
cāturvarṇyaṃ tu devānāṃ te cāpy ekatra bhuñjate
na bhokṣye sahitas tais tu tato bhokṣyāmy ahaṃ pṛthak //
34.d:
रुद्र उवाच
चातुर्वर्ण्यं तु देवानां ते चाप्य् एकत्र भुञ्जते
न भोक्ष्ये सहितस् तैस् तु ततो भोक्ष्याम्य् अहं पृथक् ॥
34.m: Rudra said: / “The gods have four classes, and they eat together; / I will not eat together with them, but I will eat separately.

34.s:
sarveṣāṃ caiva lokānām ādir bhūrloka ucyate
tam ahaṃ dhārayāmy ekaḥ svecchayā na tavājñayā //
34.d:
सर्वेषां चैव लोकानाम् आदिर् भूर्लोक उच्यते
तम् अहं धारयाम्य् एकः स्वेच्छया न तवाज्ञया ॥
34.m: The earth world is said to be the beginning of all the worlds; / that I alone sustain of my own will, not by your command.

34.s:
tasmin dhṛte sarvalokāḥ sarve tiṣṭhanti śāśvatāḥ
tasmād ahaṃ vasāmīha satataṃ na tavājñayā //
34.d:
तस्मिन् धृते सर्वलोकाः सर्वे तिष्ठन्ति शाश्वताः
तस्माद् अहं वसामीह सततं न तवाज्ञया ॥
34.m: When that is sustained, all worlds remain eternal; / therefore I dwell here constantly, not by your command.”

34.s:
brahmovāca
tato 'bhivyāhṛto dakṣo rudreṇāmitatejasā
svāyaṃbhuvīṃ tanuṃ tyaktvā utpanno mānuṣeṣv iha //
34.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततो ऽभिव्याहृतो दक्षो रुद्रेणामिततेजसा
स्वायंभुवीं तनुं त्यक्त्वा उत्पन्नो मानुषेष्व् इह ॥
34.m: Brahmā said: / Then Dakṣa, cursed by Rudra of unmeasured splendour, / having abandoned his Svāyambhuva body, was born here among mortals.

34.s:
yadā gṛhapatir dakṣo yajñānām īśvaraḥ prabhuḥ
samasteneha yajñena so 'yajad daivataiḥ saha //
34.d:
यदा गृहपतिर् दक्षो यज्ञानाम् ईश्वरः प्रभुः
समस्तेनेह यज्ञेन सो ऽयजद् दैवतैः सह ॥
34.m: When Dakṣa, the householder, the lord and ruler of sacrifices, / sacrificed here with a complete sacrifice along with the deities,

34.s:
atha devī satī yat te prāpte vaivasvate 'ntare
menāyāṃ tām umāṃ devīṃ janayām āsa śailarāṭ //
34.d:
अथ देवी सती यत् ते प्राप्ते वैवस्वते ऽन्तरे
मेनायां ताम् उमां देवीं जनयाम् आस शैलराट् ॥
34.m: then the goddess Satī—when the Vaivasvata interval arrived— / the king of mountains begot as the goddess Umā upon Menā.

34.s:
sā tu devī satī pūrvam āsīt paścād umābhavat
sahavratā bhavasyaiṣā naitayā mucyate bhavaḥ //
34.d:
सा तु देवी सती पूर्वम् आसीत् पश्चाद् उमाभवत्
सहव्रता भवस्यैषा नैतया मुच्यते भवः ॥
34.m: She who was previously the goddess Satī later became Umā; / sharing Bhava's vows, she is never abandoned by Bhava,

34.s:
yāvad icchati saṃsthānaṃ prabhur manvantareṣv iha
mārīcaṃ kaśyapaṃ devī yathāditir anuvratā //
34.d:
यावद् इच्छति संस्थानं प्रभुर् मन्वन्तरेष्व् इह
मारीचं कश्यपं देवी यथादितिर् अनुव्रता ॥
34.m: as long as the lord desires to abide here throughout the manvantaras, / just as the goddess Aditi is devoted to Kaśyapa, son of Marīci,

34.s:
sārdhaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ śrīs tu maghavantaṃ śacī yathā
viṣṇuṃ kīrtir uṣā sūryaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ cāpy arundhatī //
34.d:
सार्धं नारायणं श्रीस् तु मघवन्तं शची यथा
विष्णुं कीर्तिर् उषा सूर्यं वसिष्ठं चाप्य् अरुन्धती ॥
34.m: and Śrī to Nārāyaṇa, Śacī to Maghavan, / Kīrti to Viṣṇu, Uṣā to Sūrya, and Arundhatī to Vasiṣṭha.

34.s:
naitāṃs tu vijahaty etā bhartṝn devyaḥ kathaṃcana
evaṃ prācetaso dakṣo jajñe vai cākṣuṣe 'ntare //
34.d:
नैतांस् तु विजहत्य् एता भर्तॄन् देव्यः कथंचन
एवं प्राचेतसो दक्षो जज्ञे वै चाक्षुषे ऽन्तरे ॥
34.m: These goddesses never abandon their husbands in any way. / Thus Dakṣa, son of the Pracetas, was born in the Cākṣuṣa interval,

34.s:
prācīnabarhiṣaḥ pautraḥ putraś cāpi pracetasām
daśabhyas tu pracetobhyo māriṣāyāṃ punar nṛpa //
34.d:
प्राचीनबर्हिषः पौत्रः पुत्रश् चापि प्रचेतसाम्
दशभ्यस् तु प्रचेतोभ्यो मारिषायां पुनर् नृप ॥
34.m: the grandson of Prācīnabarhis and the son of the Pracetases, / from the ten Pracetases upon Māriṣā once again, O king.

34.s:
jajñe rudrābhiśāpena dvitīyam iti naḥ śrutam
bhṛgvādayas tu te sarve jajñire vai maharṣayaḥ //
34.d:
जज्ञे रुद्राभिशापेन द्वितीयम् इति नः श्रुतम्
भृग्वादयस् तु ते सर्वे जज्ञिरे वै महर्षयः ॥
34.m: He was born a second time by Rudra's curse; so we have heard. / And all those great sages, Bhṛgu and the others, were born

34.s:
ādye tretāyuge pūrvaṃ manor vaivasvatasya ha
devasya mahato yajñe vāruṇīṃ bibhratas tanum //
34.d:
आद्ये त्रेतायुगे पूर्वं मनोर् वैवस्वतस्य ह
देवस्य महतो यज्ञे वारुणीं बिभ्रतस् तनुम् ॥
34.m: in the first Tretāyuga formerly, of the Vaivasvata Manu, / at the sacrifice of the great god who assumed the form of Varuṇa.

34.s:
ity eṣo 'nuśayo hy āsīt tayor jātyantare gataḥ
prajāpateś ca dakṣasya tryambakasya ca dhīmataḥ //
34.d:
इत्य् एषो ऽनुशयो ह्य् आसीत् तयोर् जात्यन्तरे गतः
प्रजापतेश् च दक्षस्य त्र्यम्बकस्य च धीमतः ॥
34.m: Thus this enmity passed into another birth for the two of them, / for the lord of creatures Dakṣa and for the wise Tryambaka.

34.s:
tasmān nānuśayaḥ kāryo vareṣv iha kadācana
jātyantaragatasyāpi bhāvitasya śubhāśubhaiḥ
jantor na bhūtaye khyātis tan na kāryaṃ vijānatā //
34.d:
तस्मान् नानुशयः कार्यो वरेष्व् इह कदाचन
जात्यन्तरगतस्यापि भावितस्य शुभाशुभैः
जन्तोर् न भूतये ख्यातिस् तन् न कार्यं विजानता ॥
34.m: Therefore enmity should never be held toward sons-in-law here; / even for one gone to another birth, conditioned by good and bad deeds, / it does not bring prosperity to a living being; so a wise person should not do it.

34.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
kathaṃ roṣeṇa sā pūrvaṃ dakṣasya duhitā satī
tyaktvā dehaṃ punar jātā girirājagṛhe prabho //
34.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
कथं रोषेण सा पूर्वं दक्षस्य दुहिता सती
त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर् जाता गिरिराजगृहे प्रभो ॥
34.m: The sages said: / How did that daughter of Dakṣa, Satī, having abandoned her body in anger / in the past, get born again in the house of the king of mountains, O lord?

34.s:
dehāntare kathaṃ tasyāḥ pūrvadeho babhūva ha
bhavena saha saṃyogaḥ saṃvādaś ca tayoḥ katham //
34.d:
देहान्तरे कथं तस्याः पूर्वदेहो बभूव ह
भवेन सह संयोगः संवादश् च तयोः कथम् ॥
34.m: How, in another body, did she regain her former body? / How was her union with Bhava, and how was their conversation?

34.s:
svayaṃvaraḥ kathaṃ vṛttas tasmin mahati janmani
vivāhaś ca jagannātha sarvāścaryasamanvitaḥ //
34.d:
स्वयंवरः कथं वृत्तस् तस्मिन् महति जन्मनि
विवाहश् च जगन्नाथ सर्वाश्चर्यसमन्वितः ॥
34.m: How did the self-choice happen in that great birth, / and the wedding, O lord of the world, full of all wonders?

34.s:
tat sarvaṃ vistarād brahman vaktum arhasi sāṃpratam
śrotum icchāmahe puṇyāṃ kathāṃ cātimanoharām //
34.d:
तत् सर्वं विस्तराद् ब्रह्मन् वक्तुम् अर्हसि सांप्रतम्
श्रोतुम् इच्छामहे पुण्यां कथां चातिमनोहराम् ॥
34.m: You ought to tell all that in detail now, O Brahmā; / we wish to hear that holy and most charming story.

34.s:
brahmovāca
śṛṇudhvaṃ muniśārdūlāḥ kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm
umāśaṃkarayoḥ puṇyāṃ sarvakāmaphalapradām //
34.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
शृणुध्वं मुनिशार्दूलाः कथां पापप्रणाशिनीम्
उमाशंकरयोः पुण्यां सर्वकामफलप्रदाम् ॥
34.m: Brahmā said: / Listen, O tigers among sages, to the story that destroys sins, / the holy [story] of Umā and Śaṅkara, which grants the fruits of all desires.

34.s:
kadācit svagṛhāt prāptaṃ kaśyapaṃ dvipadāṃ varam
apṛcchad dhimavān vṛttaṃ loke khyātikaraṃ hitam //
34.d:
कदाचित् स्वगृहात् प्राप्तं कश्यपं द्विपदां वरम्
अपृच्छद् धिमवान् वृत्तं लोके ख्यातिकरं हितम् ॥
34.m: Once Himavat asked Kaśyapa, the best of two-legged beings, who had arrived at his home, / about the conduct in the world that brings renown and welfare:

34.s:
kenākṣayāś ca lokāḥ syuḥ khyātiś ca paramā mune
tathaiva cārcanīyatvaṃ satsu tat kathayasva me //
34.d:
केनाक्षयाश् च लोकाः स्युः ख्यातिश् च परमा मुने
तथैव चार्चनीयत्वं सत्सु तत् कथयस्व मे ॥
34.m: “By what means would the worlds be imperishable, O sage, and highest renown [attained], / and likewise worshipfulness among the virtuous? Tell me that.”

34.s:
kaśyapa uvāca
apatyena mahābāho sarvam etad avāpyate
mamākhyātir apatyena brahmaṇā ṛṣibhiḥ saha //
34.d:
कश्यप उवाच
अपत्येन महाबाहो सर्वम् एतद् अवाप्यते
ममाख्यातिर् अपत्येन ब्रह्मणा ऋषिभिः सह ॥
34.m: Kaśyapa said: / “By offspring, O mighty-armed one, all this is attained; / my renown is through offspring, along with Brahmā and the sages.

34.s:
kiṃ na paśyasi śailendra yato māṃ paripṛcchasi
vartayiṣyāmi yac cāpi yathādṛṣṭaṃ purācala //
34.d:
किं न पश्यसि शैलेन्द्र यतो मां परिपृच्छसि
वर्तयिष्यामि यच् चापि यथादृष्टं पुराचल ॥
34.m: Do you not see, O lord of mountains, that you ask me? / I shall also relate what was seen by me long ago, O mountain.

34.s:
vārāṇasīm ahaṃ gacchann apaśyaṃ saṃsthitaṃ divi
vimānaṃ sunavaṃ divyam anaupamyaṃ mahardhimat //
34.d:
वाराणसीम् अहं गच्छन्न् अपश्यं संस्थितं दिवि
विमानं सुनवं दिव्यम् अनौपम्यं महर्धिमत् ॥
34.m: Going to Vārāṇasī, I saw standing in the sky / a celestial, brand-new aerial chariot, matchless and of great splendour.

34.s:
tasyādhastād ārtanādaṃ gartasthāne śṛṇomy aham
tam ahaṃ tapasā jñātvā tatraivāntarhitaḥ sthitaḥ //
34.d:
तस्याधस्ताद् आर्तनादं गर्तस्थाने शृणोम्य् अहम्
तम् अहं तपसा ज्ञात्वा तत्रैवान्तर्हितः स्थितः ॥
34.m: Beneath it, in a pit, I heard a cry of distress. / Knowing that by means of austerity, I remained there, concealed.

34.s:
athāgāt tatra śailendra vipro niyamavāñ śuciḥ
tīrthābhiṣekapūtātmā pare tapasi saṃsthitaḥ //
34.d:
अथागात् तत्र शैलेन्द्र विप्रो नियमवाञ् शुचिः
तीर्थाभिषेकपूतात्मा परे तपसि संस्थितः ॥
34.m: Then, O lord of mountains, a pure brahmin of strict vows arrived there, / his self purified by bathing at holy sites, established in supreme austerity.

34.s:
atha sa vrajamānas tu vyāghreṇābhīṣito dvijaḥ
viveśa taṃ tadā deśaṃ sa garto yatra bhūdhara //
34.d:
अथ स व्रजमानस् तु व्याघ्रेणाभीषितो द्विजः
विवेश तं तदा देशं स गर्तो यत्र भूधर ॥
34.m: Then, as he was walking, that twice-born, frightened by a tiger, / entered that place, O mountain, where that pit was located.

34.s:
gartāyāṃ vīraṇastambe lambamānāṃs tadā munīn
apaśyad ārto duḥkhārtāṃs tān apṛcchac ca sa dvijaḥ //
34.d:
गर्तायां वीरणस्तम्बे लम्बमानांस् तदा मुनीन्
अपश्यद् आर्तो दुःखार्तांस् तान् अपृच्छच् च स द्विजः ॥
34.m: There in the pit he saw sages hanging from a clump of vīraṇa grass, / afflicted and suffering; and the twice-born asked them:

34.s:
dvija uvāca
ke yūyaṃ vīraṇastambe lambamānā hy adhomukhāḥ
duḥkhitāḥ kena mokṣaś ca yuṣmākaṃ bhavitānaghāḥ //
34.d:
द्विज उवाच
के यूयं वीरणस्तम्बे लम्बमाना ह्य् अधोमुखाः
दुःखिताः केन मोक्षश् च युष्माकं भवितानघाः ॥
34.m: The twice-born said: / 'Who are you, hanging head downwards from this clump of vīraṇa grass, / suffering? By what means will there be liberation for you, sinless ones?'

34.s:
pitara ūcuḥ
vayaṃ te kṛtapuṇyasya pitaraḥ sapitāmahāḥ
prapitāmahāś ca kliśyāmas tava duṣṭena karmaṇā //
34.d:
पितर ऊचुः
वयं ते कृतपुण्यस्य पितरः सपितामहाः
प्रपितामहाश् च क्लिश्यामस् तव दुष्टेन कर्मणा ॥
34.m: The ancestors said: / 'We are your ancestors, along with your grandfathers / and great-grandfathers, meritorious one; we are tormented because of your wicked deed.

34.s:
narako 'yaṃ mahābhāga gartarūpeṇa saṃsthitaḥ
tvaṃ cāpi vīraṇastambas tvayi lambāmahe vayam //
34.d:
नरको ऽयं महाभाग गर्तरूपेण संस्थितः
त्वं चापि वीरणस्तम्बस् त्वयि लम्बामहे वयम् ॥
34.m: This is hell, O fortunate one, present in the form of a pit; / and you are the clump of vīraṇa grass upon which we hang.

34.s:
yāvat tvaṃ jīvase vipra tāvad eva vayaṃ sthitāḥ
mṛte tvayi gamiṣyāmo narakaṃ pāpacetasaḥ //
34.d:
यावत् त्वं जीवसे विप्र तावद् एव वयं स्थिताः
मृते त्वयि गमिष्यामो नरकं पापचेतसः ॥
34.m: As long as you live, O twice-born, just so long do we remain [suspended]; / when you die, we, whose minds are sinful, will go to hell.

34.s:
yadi tvaṃ dārasaṃyogaṃ kṛtvāpatyaṃ guṇottaram
utpādayasi tenāsmān mucyema vayam enasaḥ //
34.d:
यदि त्वं दारसंयोगं कृत्वापत्यं गुणोत्तरम्
उत्पादयसि तेनास्मान् मुच्येम वयम् एनसः ॥
34.m: If you unite with a wife and beget / an offspring endowed with superior virtues, we shall thereby be freed from sin.

34.s:
nānyena tapasā putra tīrthānāṃ ca phalena ca
etat kuru mahābuddhe tārayasva pitṝn bhayāt //
34.d:
नान्येन तपसा पुत्र तीर्थानां च फलेन च
एतत् कुरु महाबुद्धे तारयस्व पितॄन् भयात् ॥
